news.title: Guangzhou Internet Finance Crackdown Enters Enforcement Phase
news.body: Southern Metropolis Daily reports that Guangzhou has launched a special campaign against internet finance, screening P2P lending platforms and clearing out non-compliant ones.

news.title: Persistent Rain in the Middle and Lower Yangtze Leaves Several Provinces Flooded
news.body: The National Meteorological Center has issued rainstorm warnings repeatedly as severe flooding hits Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu and other areas along the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze, leaving millions affected and the flood control situation grave.

news.title: Portugal Beat France 1-0 to Win First European Championship
news.body: In the Euro 2016 final at the Stade de France, Portugal beat hosts France 1-0 through substitute Eder's long-range strike in the 109th minute of extra time to claim the European Championship for the first time in their history.

news.title: G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting Closes in Shanghai
news.body: The G20 trade ministers' meeting closed in Shanghai after adopting the first statement by G20 trade ministers in the group's history, agreeing to strengthen the multilateral trading system and advance a strategy for global trade growth.

news.title: Truck Attack in Nice, France Kills 84
news.body: In the early hours of July 15 Beijing time, a truck deliberately plowed into a crowd in the southern French city of Nice after Bastille Day fireworks, killing 84 people and injuring dozens; an extremist group later claimed responsibility for the attack.

news.title: Zhao Wei's New Film Replaces Male Lead Leon Dai
news.body: The producers of Zhao Wei's film 'No Other Love' announced that they were replacing male lead Leon Dai, saying his political stance had caused controversy for the film; Zhao Wei subsequently apologized, and the episode set off heated discussion across the internet.

news.title: Xiaomi Launches Redmi Pro and Mi Notebook Air
news.body: At a launch event in Beijing, Xiaomi officially unveiled its dual-camera Redmi Pro and released the Mi Notebook Air, the company's first laptop, further expanding its product line.

news.title: Sustained Heat Pushes Temperatures Above 39C in Southern China
news.body: The National Meteorological Center issued an orange heat alert for several days running as maximum temperatures in Shanghai, Jiangsu and Zhejiang topped 39C, power grid loads hit record highs and multiple government departments activated heat emergency responses.

news.title: China Marks 40th Anniversary of the Tangshan Earthquake
news.body: On July 28, the 40th anniversary of the 1976 Tangshan earthquake, a wreath-laying ceremony was held at the Tangshan Earthquake Memorial Square, where people from all walks of life commemorated the more than 240,000 victims and looked back on the city's reconstruction.

news.title: Fed Leaves Benchmark Interest Rate Unchanged
news.body: The Federal Reserve concluded its July policy meeting by leaving the federal funds rate in a range of 0.25% to 0.5%, saying the timing of a rate rise would depend on employment and inflation data.

news.title: Hillary Clinton Formally Accepts Democratic Presidential Nomination
news.body: The Democratic National Convention wrapped up in Philadelphia, where Hillary Clinton delivered a speech formally accepting the party's presidential nomination and became the first woman in US history to win a major party's presidential nomination.

news.title: Nintendo's Pokemon GO Tops 100 Million Downloads Worldwide
news.body: Pokemon GO, the augmented-reality mobile game developed by Nintendo and Niantic, kept exploding in popularity around the world, passing 100 million downloads within three weeks of release as Nintendo's share price briefly soared.

news.title: Didi Chuxing Announces Acquisition of Uber China
news.body: Didi Chuxing announced a strategic agreement with Uber Global to acquire all of Uber China's assets, including its brand, operations and data, with Uber Global to hold a 5.89% stake in Didi, upending the landscape of China's ride-hailing market.

news.title: Yuriko Koike Elected Tokyo's First Female Governor
news.body: Former defence minister Yuriko Koike won the Tokyo gubernatorial election, becoming the first woman to serve as governor in the Japanese capital's history; she said she would work to advance preparations for the Tokyo Olympics and to reform the city.

news.title: Film 'Time Raiders' Opens Nationwide
news.body: Adapted from the novel of the same name by Nanpai Sanshu and starring Lu Han and Jing Boran, the film 'Time Raiders' opened nationwide, taking more than 200 million yuan on its first day and setting off a summer box office rush.

news.title: China's Rio Olympic Delegation Holds Flag-Raising Ceremony
news.body: China's sports delegation for the Rio Olympics held a flag-raising ceremony in the Olympic Village, with a contingent of 416 athletes taking part - the largest Chinese delegation ever sent to an Olympics held abroad.

news.title: 'Love O2O' Wins Praise on Release
news.body: Adapted from Gu Man's novel of the same name and starring Angelababy and Jing Boran, the film 'Love O2O' opened nationwide, earning more than 200 million yuan in its first weekend and emerging as the surprise romance hit of the summer.

news.title: Death Toll From Hubei Dangyang Power Plant Pipe Blast Rises to 21
news.body: A high-pressure steam pipe burst at Madian Coal Gangue Power Generation Co. in Dangyang, Hubei, raising the death toll to 21 with five injured; the Work Safety Committee of the State Council has placed the investigation under special supervision.

news.title: China's Women's Volleyball Team Beats Brazil 3-2 to Reach Olympic Semifinals
news.body: In the women's volleyball quarterfinals at the Rio Olympics, China came from a set down to beat hosts and defending champions Brazil 3-2 after a five-set battle, advancing to the semifinals as the home crowd fell silent.

news.title: Russia Uses Iranian Base for Syria Airstrikes for First Time
news.body: Russian Tu-22M3 bombers took off from Hamadan Air Base in Iran for the first time to strike extremist targets inside Syria - Russia's first military operation launched from Iranian territory - drawing intense international attention.

news.title: National Health Conference Held in Beijing
news.body: The National Health Conference was held in Beijing on August 19 and 20, calling for people's health to be given strategic priority in development and for all-round, full-lifecycle protection of public health.

news.title: Brazilian Police Announce Findings in Lochte False Robbery Claim
news.body: Brazilian police released the conclusions of their investigation, finding that US swimming star Ryan Lochte's claim to have been robbed at gunpoint in Rio was false; Lochte apologized publicly and several sponsors subsequently dropped him.

news.title: Four Departments Issue Interim Online Lending Rules With 13 Red Lines
news.body: The China Banking Regulatory Commission, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the Ministry of Public Security and the Cyberspace Administration of China jointly issued interim measures governing the business activities of online lending information intermediaries, establishing a regulatory framework for the P2P lending industry and setting 13 red lines, including bans on taking public deposits and on operating fund pools.

news.title: Magnitude-6.2 Quake in Central Italy Kills Nearly 300
news.body: A magnitude-6.2 earthquake struck the Lazio region of central Italy, devastating the historic town of Amatrice and killing nearly 300 people as rescuers searched the rubble for survivors.

news.title: Hangzhou Ready for G20 Summit as World Watches
news.body: On the eve of the G20 Hangzhou summit, all preparations were complete and environmental upgrades at the West Lake scenic area had been finished, with leaders of the world's major economies and heads of international organizations arriving in Hangzhou as the global media focused on China.

news.title: Events Marking 80th Anniversary of the Long March Launch
news.body: Events marking the 80th anniversary of the Red Army's Long March got under way across the country, commemorating revolutionary martyrs and carrying forward the spirit of the Long March through activities such as retracing the route and themed exhibitions.

news.title: China Draws 0-0 With Iran for First Point in Final Qualifying Round
news.body: In the second round of matches in the final round of Asian qualifying for the 2018 World Cup, which features 12 teams, China drew 0-0 with Iran, Asia's top-ranked team, at the Shenyang Olympic Sports Center, earning their first point of the stage as tens of thousands of fans sang the national anthem in support.

news.title: Hangzhou G20 Summit Closes With Multiple Points of Consensus
news.body: The closely watched G20 Hangzhou summit drew to a close after adopting the G20 Leaders' Communique, reaching consensus on strengthening macroeconomic policy coordination, innovating growth models and revitalizing international trade and investment.

news.title: China's First Quantum Satellite Progresses Through In-Orbit Tests
news.body: Since its launch on August 16, the Micius satellite, the world's first quantum science experiment satellite, has been progressing smoothly through in-orbit testing, laying the groundwork for subsequent satellite-to-ground quantum communication experiments.

news.title: Hong Kong Legislative Council Election Results Announced
news.body: Results of the election to the sixth Legislative Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region were announced, with all 70 seats filled and more than 2.2 million voters casting ballots, a record turnout.

news.title: Apple Event Spotlights the iPhone 7
news.body: Apple unveiled the iPhone 7 and iPhone 7 Plus on September 7, dropping the traditional 3.5mm headphone jack, adding water resistance and a dual camera, and introducing the wireless AirPods to widespread discussion.

news.title: Typhoon Meranti Bears Down on Southeast Coast
news.body: This year's 14th typhoon, Meranti, rapidly intensified into a super typhoon and closed in on the coasts of Taiwan and Fujian; the State Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters activated a flood and typhoon emergency response and ordered coastal areas to prepare.

news.title: Meranti Devastates Xiamen and Quanzhou, Causing Heavy Losses
news.body: Super Typhoon Meranti made landfall on the coast of Xiang'an in Xiamen, Fujian, just before the Mid-Autumn Festival with maximum winds near its centre reaching force 15, devastating Xiamen, Quanzhou and nearby areas, leaving dozens dead or missing and causing more than 10 billion yuan in direct economic losses.

news.title: North Korea Conducts Largest Nuclear Test to Date
news.body: North Korea announced the successful conduct of its fifth nuclear test, which South Korea's meteorological agency measured as a magnitude-5.0 seismic event; it was Pyongyang's largest test to date, prompting strong international condemnation and calls for tougher sanctions.

news.title: Ministry of Education Orders Campus Lending Risk Campaign
news.body: The General Office of the Ministry of Education issued a notice launching a nationwide awareness campaign at universities on the risks of campus online lending, requiring institutions to teach students about credit and financial risk and to guard against predatory campus loans.

news.title: Shenzhen's Six-Square-Metre 'Pigeon Cage' Flats Halted and Investigated
news.body: The Shenzhen planning and land commission reported that it had investigated the illegal sale of six-square-metre 'pigeon cage' units at the Qiaocheng Shangyu project and ordered the relevant purchase agreements to be cancelled; the tiny flats with sky-high prices laid bare anxiety over housing costs in first-tier cities and sparked heated discussion online.

news.title: Fan Zhendong Wins First Table Tennis Men's World Cup
news.body: The 2016 Table Tennis Men's World Cup concluded in Saarbrucken, Germany, where Fan Zhendong beat teammate Xu Xin 4-1 in the final to claim his first singles title at one of the sport's three major events.

news.title: National Travel Peak Hits on First Day of Golden Week
news.body: On the first day of the National Day holiday, railways carried more than 14 million passengers, a record high, while expressways were congested across the country and major scenic spots saw peak visitor flows.

news.title: Samsung Halts Global Sales and Exchanges of Note7
news.body: Samsung Electronics announced a worldwide halt to sales and exchanges of its Galaxy Note7 smartphone and told users to power the devices down immediately after a series of battery fires and explosions dealt a heavy blow to the brand.

news.title: 2016 Nobel Prize in Economics Announced
news.body: The 2016 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to US economists Oliver Hart and Bengt Holmstrom for their outstanding contributions to contract theory.

news.title: State Council Publishes Internet Finance Risk Plan
news.body: The General Office of the State Council published a work plan for a special campaign against internet finance risks, led by the People's Bank of China with 17 departments taking part, imposing look-through supervision on P2P lending, equity crowdfunding and online insurance and resolving risks by category.

news.title: Shenzhou-11 Manned Mission Enters Final Stretch
news.body: A full-scale joint rehearsal was held for the Shenzhou-11 manned mission, with the spacecraft due to launch in mid-October; two astronauts will take up a 30-day stay aboard the Tiangong-2 space laboratory, setting a new record for China's time in orbit.

news.title: Meeting Marking 80th Anniversary of Long March Victory Held in Beijing
news.body: A grand meeting marking the 80th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, where Xi Jinping delivered an important speech stressing that each generation has its own Long March to walk and must walk today's well.

news.title: Iraqi Forces Launch Offensive to Retake Mosul
news.body: Backed by airstrikes from the US-led coalition, Iraqi government forces launched a major offensive on Mosul, the stronghold of an extremist group, in Iraq's largest military operation in years as tens of thousands of civilians fled their homes.

news.title: Xiaomi Unveils Full-Screen Concept Phone Mi MIX
news.body: At a product launch in Beijing, Xiaomi introduced the dual-curved flagship Mi Note 2 and the full-screen concept phone Mi MIX, whose ultra-narrow bezels stunned the audience and won praise from foreign media as China's most innovative phone.

news.title: France Begins Demolition of Calais 'Jungle' Camp
news.body: The French government deployed large numbers of police to begin dismantling the Calais 'Jungle' migrant camp, with thousands of stranded illegal migrants moved in stages to reception centres around the country as the situation in Calais touched a nerve in Europe's refugee debate.

news.title: Gas Explosion at Jinshangou Coal Mine in Chongqing's Yongchuan District
news.body: A gas explosion at the Jinshangou coal mine in Yongchuan district, Chongqing, killed all 33 miners underground; the Work Safety Committee of the State Council placed the case under special supervision, and the accident exposed serious problems including illegal production at the mine.

news.title: Zhuhai Airshow Opens With J-20 Set for Public Debut
news.body: As the 11th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition (Airshow China) prepared to open in Zhuhai, two J-20 stealth fighters were set to perform a flight display - the first public appearance of a fifth-generation fighter developed independently by China - drawing worldwide attention.

news.title: Long March 5 Rocket Makes Successful Maiden Flight
news.body: China's most powerful new-generation launch vehicle, the Long March 5, lifted off from the Wenchang Space Launch Center in Hainan and completed a successful maiden flight, marking China's entry into the front ranks of launch vehicle capability.

news.title: Paris Agreement Enters Into Force
news.body: The Paris Agreement entered into force on the first anniversary of its adoption, becoming one of the fastest international treaties ever to take effect and taking global cooperation on climate change into a new phase.

news.title: Trump Defeats Clinton to Win US Presidency
news.body: Results of the US presidential election showed Republican candidate Donald Trump defeating Democratic candidate Hillary Clinton to become the 45th president of the United States, with global financial markets stabilizing after sharp overnight swings.

news.title: Red Fog Alerts Issued as Expressways Close
news.body: North China, the Huang-Huai region and other areas were hit by widespread smog and dense fog, forcing the closure of multiple expressways and the suspension of outdoor activities at primary and secondary schools and kindergartens as the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region activated heavy pollution emergency responses.

news.title: Magnitude-7.8 Quake in New Zealand's South Island Triggers Tsunami Alert
news.body: A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck the central South Island of New Zealand, severely damaging the small town of Kaikoura near the epicentre; the quake triggered localized tsunamis, trapping thousands of tourists and residents, and the prime minister declared a state of emergency.

news.title: Internet Finance Campaign Moves Into Cleanup Phase
news.body: Under the work plan for the special campaign against internet finance risks, screening has been largely completed nationwide and the campaign has officially moved into its cleanup and rectification phase, in which non-compliant lending platforms will be ordered to make corrections within a deadline or be shut down in accordance with the law.

news.title: Lippi's China Held to Draw by Qatar in Coaching Debut
news.body: In the fifth round of matches in the final round of Asian qualifying for the 2018 World Cup, which features 12 teams, new coach Marcello Lippi made his debut in charge of the Chinese men's national team, who drew 0-0 with Qatar at home in Kunming; China dominated but hit the woodwork several times and were left ruing the two dropped points.

news.title: Supermoon Lights Up Skies as Biggest in Nearly 70 Years
news.body: The largest and brightest supermoon of the century so far appeared in skies around the world, with the Moon at its closest to Earth since 1948; astronomy enthusiasts everywhere photographed the rare spectacle, and the next supermoon this large will not come until 2034.

news.title: Shenzhou-11 Return Capsule Lands Safely
news.body: The return capsule of the Shenzhou-11 spacecraft landed safely in its designated area in central Inner Mongolia, with astronauts Jing Haipeng and Chen Dong in good health after completing a 33-day stay in space that set a record for the longest time a Chinese astronaut has spent in orbit.

news.title: Feng Xiaogang's 'I Am Not Madame Bovary' Opens
news.body: Directed by Feng Xiaogang and starring Fan Bingbing, 'I Am Not Madame Bovary' opened nationwide, drawing widespread discussion for its circular framing and earning Fan Bingbing the best actress award at the San Sebastian International Film Festival.

news.title: Magnitude-7.4 Quake Off Fukushima Triggers Tsunami Alert
news.body: A magnitude-7.4 earthquake struck off the coast near Fukushima, Japan, at a depth of about 10 kilometres; the Japan Meteorological Agency issued tsunami advisories for Fukushima, Miyagi and other areas, no abnormalities were found at the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant, and bullet train services were suspended in several regions.

news.title: Cooling Tower Platform Collapse at Jiangxi Fengcheng Power Plant Kills 74
news.body: A construction platform on a cooling tower at the Phase III expansion of the Fengcheng power plant in Jiangxi collapsed, killing 74 workers; the State Council set up an investigation team to establish the cause, and a number of those responsible were taken into custody in accordance with the law.

news.title: 'Naked Loan' Scandal Exposes Campus Lending Risks
news.body: Media exposed 'naked loans' in which female university students used nude photos of themselves holding their ID cards as collateral; Jiedaibao announced it had frozen the accounts involved and was assisting police, while the China Banking Regulatory Commission and other authorities again warned of the risks of predatory campus lending and barred online lenders from issuing loans to students in violation of the rules.

news.title: Reversal in Luo Er's Fundraising for Daughter Prompts Soul-Searching
news.body: Luo Er, a Shenzhen resident, raised more than 2 million yuan in reader donations after writing about his daughter's leukaemia, only for internet users to reveal that he owned several properties and had worked with a marketing company to stoke sympathy; the twists and turns of the case set off a nationwide debate about honesty in online fundraising.

news.title: Pakistan International Airlines Crash Kills 47
news.body: A Pakistan International Airlines ATR-42 aircraft crashed near Havelian in the north of the country, killing all 47 people on board; the aircraft's black boxes were recovered and Pakistani authorities opened an investigation.

news.title: Alipay Begins Charging Fees on Cash Withdrawals
news.body: Alipay began applying its free-quota policy to personal cash withdrawals, charging a 0.1% service fee on amounts above the 20,000 yuan free allowance, a new fee policy from the mobile payments giant that prompted widespread discussion among users.

news.title: National Memorial Held for Nanjing Massacre Victims
news.body: The third national memorial ceremony for the victims of the Nanjing Massacre was held at the Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders, where representatives from all walks of life commemorated the 300,000 victims, remembered history and prayed for peace.

news.title: Major Turning Point in the Battle for Aleppo
news.body: Backed by Russian airstrikes, Syrian government forces recaptured large areas of eastern Aleppo, sharply shrinking the territory held by rebel forces; the battle for Aleppo, now more than four years old, reached a major turning point as tens of thousands of civilians fled.

news.title: Fed Raises Rates by 25 Basis Points
news.body: The Federal Reserve concluded its last monetary policy meeting of the year by raising the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 0.5%-0.75% and projecting three rate increases in 2017; it was the Fed's first hike in a year and markets reacted sharply.

news.title: Air Quality Worsens Nationwide as Provinces Issue Red Alerts
news.body: Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and surrounding areas suffered their worst heavy pollution episode of the year, with many cities issuing red alerts for heavy pollution, schools suspending classes and vehicles restricted; the Ministry of Environmental Protection sent inspection teams to supervise the implementation of emergency measures.

news.title: Cavaliers Edge Warriors 109-108 in NBA Christmas Game
news.body: In the marquee NBA Christmas Day matchup, the Cavaliers beat the Warriors 109-108 on the road as Kyrie Irving scored repeatedly late to seal the win, rekindling the rivalry from the Finals.

news.title: Defence Ministry Confirms First Home-Built Aircraft Carrier Under Construction
news.body: At its regular press conference, the Ministry of National Defense said China's first domestically built aircraft carrier was under smooth construction as planned - the first carrier designed and built by China itself - drawing wide attention at home and abroad.

news.title: Ride-Hailing Rules Take Effect in Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen
news.body: Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen and other cities formally issued rules for ride-hailing services covering vehicle wheelbase, engine displacement and drivers' household registration, taking the industry into a new phase of regulated development, though differences in how strictly cities enforce them have prompted debate.

news.title: Russian Tu-154 Crashes Into Black Sea, Killing 92
news.body: A Tu-154 aircraft of the Russian Defence Ministry crashed into the Black Sea near Sochi, killing all 92 people on board, including members of the renowned Alexandrov Ensemble; Russia declared December 26 a national day of mourning.

news.title: New Year's Eve Attack on Istanbul Nightclub Kills 39
news.body: A gunman attacked an upmarket nightclub in central Istanbul during New Year celebrations, killing 39 people and injuring nearly 70; an extremist group later claimed responsibility for the attack.

news.title: Web Drama 'Candle in the Tomb: The Ancient City' Draws Huge Audiences
news.body: The web drama 'Candle in the Tomb: The Ancient City', adapted from Zhang Muye's novel of the same name and starring Jin Dong and Joe Chen, drew huge audiences, winning praise from fans of the original for its polished production and drawing billions of views.

news.title: US Congress Certifies Trump's Presidential Victory
news.body: The two chambers of the US Congress met in a joint session to formally certify Donald Trump's victory in the 2016 presidential election, clearing the last procedural hurdle before his inauguration on January 20.

news.title: Heavy Pollution Blankets North China Over New Year as Alerts Escalate
news.body: North China and surrounding areas endured heavy pollution over the New Year holiday, with many places in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region maintaining orange alerts or higher; at times air quality readings in Shijiazhuang went off the scale, and school closures and vehicle restrictions continued.

news.title: WeChat Mini Programs Officially Launch
news.body: Tencent officially launched its WeChat Mini Program platform, letting users access apps without downloading or installing them; Zhang Xiaolong described mini programs as a new kind of app that can be used and left, sending shockwaves through the mobile internet industry.

news.title: National Science and Technology Awards Ceremony Held in Beijing
news.body: The 2016 National Science and Technology Awards ceremony was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, where physicist Zhao Zhongxian and pharmacologist Tu Youyou jointly received the State Preeminent Science and Technology Award.

news.title: Banking Regulator Vows Deeper Internet Finance Cleanup and Crackdown on Campus Loans
news.body: The China Banking Regulatory Commission held its 2017 national conference on banking supervision, pledging to deepen the special campaign against internet finance risks and to crack down on campus lending, abuses in online lending and illegal fundraising.

news.title: 2017 Spring Festival Travel Rush Begins
news.body: The 40-day Spring Festival travel rush of 2017 got under way, with the total number of passenger trips nationwide expected to reach 2.978 billion as railways, airlines and highways worked to get millions of travellers home for the holiday.

news.title: Trump Sworn In as 45th US President
news.body: Donald Trump was sworn in as the 45th president of the United States at the US Capitol, delivering an inaugural address built around putting America first and bringing Barack Obama's eight years in office to a formal end.

news.title: 'Singer' Premieres and Makes Dimash a Star Overnight
news.body: Hunan TV's music competition show 'Singer' premiered, and Dimash, a young singer from Kazakhstan, astonished audiences with his extraordinary vocal range, quickly trending online and becoming a new fan favourite.

news.title: Federer Beats Nadal 3-2 for 18th Grand Slam Title
news.body: The Australian Open men's singles final delivered a classic chapter in the Federer-Nadal rivalry, with Federer beating Nadal 3-2 after a five-set battle to lift his 18th Grand Slam trophy and his fifth Australian Open title.

news.title: Trump Travel Ban Sparks Global Protests
news.body: Trump signed an executive order suspending entry to the United States by citizens of seven Muslim-majority countries, triggering protests worldwide and chaos at airports as several states and technology companies filed lawsuits against it.

news.title: Patriots Beat Falcons 34-28 in Overtime in Epic Super Bowl Comeback
news.body: Super Bowl LI in Houston produced an epic comeback as the New England Patriots, trailing 3-28 in the third quarter, scored 25 unanswered points and beat the Atlanta Falcons 34-28 in overtime, giving Tom Brady his fifth Vince Lombardi Trophy.

news.title: 'Eternal Love' Draws Over 30 Billion Views
news.body: The costume fantasy drama 'Eternal Love', starring Yang Mi and Mark Chao, dominated screens, passing 30 billion views across platforms to become the year's hottest series.

news.title: UK House of Commons Passes Brexit Bill
news.body: The House of Commons passed the Brexit bill, authorizing Prime Minister Theresa May to start the process of leaving the European Union, a key step for Britain toward exiting the bloc.

news.title: Cities Step Up H7N9 Bird Flu Prevention
news.body: Human cases of H7N9 bird flu appeared in several places during the winter and spring, prompting the National Health and Family Planning Commission to deploy prevention and control measures; some cities suspended live poultry markets and experts advised the public to avoid contact with live birds.

news.title: US Appeals Court Upholds Freeze on Trump Travel Ban
news.body: The US Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled to keep Trump's travel ban suspended, and the White House said it would keep fighting the case in the courts as the dispute over the order intensified.

news.title: Japan and US Leaders Meet to Affirm Alliance
news.body: Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe visited the United States for talks with Trump in Washington, issuing a joint statement affirming that the US-Japan alliance is the cornerstone of peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific.

news.title: Kim Jong Nam Dies in Assassination at Kuala Lumpur Airport
news.body: Kim Jong Nam, half-brother of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, was killed at Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Malaysia when two women attacked him with the VX nerve agent, setting off a fierce diplomatic row between Malaysia and North Korea.

news.title: 'La La Land' Draws Crowds in China
news.body: The Hollywood musical 'La La Land', which swept 14 Oscar nominations, opened in mainland China and drew crowds over the Valentine's Day period, its romance between Ryan Gosling and Emma Stone winning over audiences.

news.title: Samsung Vice Chairman Lee Jae-yong Arrested on Bribery Allegations
news.body: A South Korean court approved an arrest warrant for Samsung Electronics vice chairman Lee Jae-yong on suspicion of bribing Choi Soon-sil, a confidante of President Park Geun-hye, plunging the Samsung group into an unprecedented crisis.

news.title: Bike-Sharing War Intensifies as Clutter Prompts Crackdown
news.body: Mobike and ofo waged a fierce battle over deposit waivers and red-envelope subsidies, heating up competition in the bike-sharing industry, while the haphazard parking and vandalism of bicycles became a prominent problem and prompted several cities to step in with regulations.

news.title: Lotte and South Korea's Defence Ministry Sign THAAD Land Swap
news.body: Lotte Group formally signed an agreement with South Korea's defence ministry to swap land for the THAAD missile defence system, provoking strong dissatisfaction among Chinese consumers, with spontaneous boycotts of Lotte Mart in many places and a chill in China-South Korea relations.

news.title: Banking Regulator Issues Guidelines on Custody of Online Lending Funds
news.body: The China Banking Regulatory Commission formally issued guidelines on the custody of online lending funds, specifying that commercial banks act as custodians for such business and steering online lending platforms toward separate management of customer funds and their own.

news.title: Fifth Session of 12th CPPCC National Committee Opens
news.body: The fifth session of the 12th National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference opened at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, kicking off the annual two sessions as thousands of Chinese and foreign journalists focused on China's political season.

news.title: Snap Shares Jump 44% on First Day of Trading
news.body: Snap, the parent company of Snapchat, listed on the New York Stock Exchange at an issue price of $17 and closed its first day up 44%, giving it a market value of more than $34 billion and making it one of the largest US tech IPOs in years.

news.title: Park Geun-hye Removed From Office in Unanimous Ruling
news.body: South Korea's Constitutional Court unanimously upheld the National Assembly's impeachment motion, immediately removing Park Geun-hye from the presidency and making her the country's first democratically elected president to be removed from office; South Korea will hold a snap election within 60 days.

news.title: NPC Session Reviews Draft General Provisions of Civil Law
news.body: Delegations to the fifth session of the 12th National People's Congress carefully reviewed the draft General Provisions of the Civil Law, a key step in codifying China's civil code, with provisions on the protection of unborn children's interests and of personal information drawing wide attention.

news.title: China Beats South Korea 1-0 on Yu Dabao's Goal
news.body: In the sixth round of matches in the final round of Asian qualifying for the 2018 World Cup, which features 12 teams, China beat South Korea 1-0 at the Helong Sports Center in Changsha on Yu Dabao's first-half header, their first win of the stage, as Marcello Lippi's side kept alive their hopes of qualifying.

news.title: Westminster Attack Leaves Five Dead
news.body: A terrorist attack took place on Westminster Bridge and outside the Houses of Parliament in London, where a man drove a car into pedestrians and stabbed a police officer, killing five people, including a police officer, and injuring more than 40; an extremist group claimed responsibility.

news.title: Samsung Launches Galaxy S8 to Restore Flagship Reputation
news.body: Samsung Electronics held a launch event in New York to officially unveil its flagship Galaxy S8 and S8+, featuring an Infinity Display and iris recognition - a crucial product for Samsung to rebuild its reputation after the Note7 fires.

news.title: Dozens of Cities Tighten Property Rules After Beijing's March 17 Measures
news.body: After Beijing introduced its toughest-ever property measures on March 17, dozens of cities across the country followed within about ten days with tighter purchase and mortgage restrictions, bringing a new wave of intensive regulation to the housing market.

news.title: Liaocheng Case Coverage Sparks National Debate
news.body: Southern Weekly reported on the case of Yu Huan in Liaocheng, Shandong, who stabbed to death a man who had insulted his mother, and the life sentence handed down at first instance caused enormous controversy; the Supreme People's Procuratorate sent officials to Shandong to investigate, and the case prompted nationwide debate over the boundaries of justifiable defence.

news.title: Anti-Corruption Drama 'In the Name of the People' Sets Ratings Records
news.body: The anti-corruption drama 'In the Name of the People' premiered on Hunan TV, breaking new ground with its bold subject matter, showcasing veteran actors performing together and flooding the internet with memes of the character Secretary Dakang as ratings set one record after another.

news.title: Beijing Issues Fact-Finding and Rectification Requirements for Online Lenders
news.body: Beijing regulators issued requirements on factual findings and rectification to online lending platforms in their jurisdiction, listing more than 100 points to address; platforms must submit rectification plans within a deadline and report on their progress.

news.title: Britain Formally Begins Brexit Process
news.body: British Prime Minister Theresa May formally signed a letter triggering Article 50 of the Treaty of Lisbon, notifying the European Union that Britain was beginning the process of leaving, and opening two years of difficult negotiations.

news.title: Xinjiang Men's Basketball Sweeps Guangdong 4-0 for First CBA Title
news.body: In Game 4 of the CBA Finals, the Xinjiang Kashgar Ancient City team beat Guangdong 117-109 on the road to complete a 4-0 series sweep and win the franchise's first CBA championship, fulfilling Xinjiang basketball's dream of a top-league title.

news.title: US Launches Airstrikes on Syrian Air Base
news.body: The US military fired 59 Tomahawk cruise missiles from the Mediterranean at the Shayrat air base in Syria in response to a chemical weapons attack, sharply raising tensions between Russia and the United States.

news.title: Banking Regulator Targets Campus Loans With Five-Point Guideline
news.body: The China Banking Regulatory Commission issued guidelines on risk prevention and control in the banking sector that set out a five-point approach to campus lending abuses - stop, transfer, rectify, educate and guide - requiring online lenders to suspend all campus lending business and make corrections.

news.title: Establishment of Xiongan New Area Sets Off National Debate
news.body: News that Hebei's Xiongan New Area would be established dominated discussion, with the planned area covering three counties and property transactions frozen immediately; speculators who rushed to Baigou overnight were thwarted by policy, and the project, described as a task of the millennium, became a focus of nationwide debate.

news.title: United Airlines Dragging of Asian Passenger Draws Global Outrage
news.body: United Airlines had an Asian-American doctor forcibly dragged off an overbooked flight, and video of the incident drew outrage worldwide; the airline's CEO was criticized again for an initially dismissive response before finally apologizing and promising changes.

news.title: Shared Power Banks Become Investor Fad as Chen Ou and Wang Sicong Trade Barbs
news.body: Shared power banks became the latest hot bet for investors, with Jumei's Chen Ou investing in Jiedian and Wang Sicong declaring he would eat excrement if the business model succeeded, a long-distance wager that flooded social media.

news.title: China Launches First High-Throughput Communications Satellite Shijian-13
news.body: China successfully launched the Shijian-13 satellite from Xichang aboard a Long March 3B rocket; the country's first high-throughput communications satellite has more capacity than all of China's previous communications satellites combined, opening an era of satellite internet.

news.title: Bai Baihe's Alleged Extramarital Affair Dominates Trending Topics
news.body: Paparazzo Zhuo Wei reported that Bai Baihe had a secret rendezvous with a male model in Thailand, and video of the encounter set the internet alight; her husband Chen Yufan then said the two had long since divorced, and the story topped trending topics for days.

news.title: US Drops 'Mother of All Bombs' in Afghanistan
news.body: The US military dropped a GBU-43 Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb in Nangarhar province in eastern Afghanistan - the first combat use of the largest non-nuclear bomb, known as the mother of all bombs - targeting caves used by extremists.

news.title: 121st Canton Fair Opens in Guangzhou
news.body: The 121st China Import and Export Fair opened in Guangzhou, with the first phase focusing on electronics and home appliances; buyer attendance picked up, pointing to a stabilizing and improving foreign trade picture.

news.title: Tianzhou-1 Completes Automated Docking With Tiangong-2
news.body: After launching into orbit, the Tianzhou-1 cargo spacecraft successfully completed its first automated rendezvous and docking with the Tiangong-2 space laboratory, a debut for China's space station cargo transport system and a further step in the space laboratory programme.

news.title: Macron and Le Pen Advance to French Runoff
news.body: France held the first round of its presidential election, with centrist candidate Emmanuel Macron and far-right candidate Marine Le Pen leading the vote and advancing to a runoff, sending the euro higher.

news.title: May Day Holiday Draws 134 Million Domestic Tourists
news.body: China received 134 million domestic tourists during the three-day May Day holiday, generating 79.1 billion yuan in tourism revenue, with short trips, high-speed rail travel and self-driving tours the most popular ways to travel.

news.title: Four Domestic Films Compete Over May Day Holiday
news.body: The May Day holiday box office saw a four-way contest among the Chinese films 'Shock Wave', 'Battle of Memories', 'This Is Not What I Expected' and 'Love Off the Cuff', with Andy Lau's crime thriller 'Shock Wave' and the mystery 'Battle of Memories' leading on reviews.

news.title: Spurs Rout Rockets 114-75 to Reach Western Conference Finals
news.body: In Game 6 of the NBA Western Conference semifinals, the Spurs crushed the Rockets 114-75 at home, a 39-point margin, to win the series 4-2 and advance to the Western Conference finals as Houston's three-point shooting went cold and sent them out of the playoffs.

news.title: Moon Jae-in Elected President of South Korea
news.body: Results of South Korea's 19th presidential election showed Democratic Party candidate Moon Jae-in winning with about 41% of the vote and moving into the Blue House, ending nearly a decade of conservative rule.

news.title: WannaCry Ransomware Outbreak Hits the Globe
news.body: The WannaCry ransomware worm spread to more than 150 countries, attacking computers at hospitals, schools and petrol stations and demanding bitcoin ransoms; campus networks at several Chinese universities and some industry systems were hit, leaving the world on edge.

news.title: 'Ode to Joy 2' Premieres to Binge-Watching Frenzy
news.body: The urban women's drama 'Ode to Joy 2' premiered, with the return of the five heroines setting off a viewing frenzy; it drew more than 500 million online views on its first day, and its music and romantic storylines sparked widespread discussion.

news.title: Central Bank Announces Fintech Committee
news.body: The People's Bank of China announced the establishment of a fintech committee, proposing to step up the use of regulatory technology and improve its ability to identify and prevent risks in new business models such as internet finance and online lending, arming financial oversight with technology.

news.title: Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation Closes in Beijing
news.body: The Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation closed in Beijing, with 29 foreign heads of state and government attending. The forum produced a list of more than 270 deliverables, and China will add 100 billion yuan in new funding to the Silk Road Fund.

news.title: US Appoints Special Counsel to Investigate Russia Ties
news.body: The US Department of Justice appointed former FBI director Robert Mueller as special counsel to fully investigate allegations that Donald Trump's campaign colluded with Russia, as the Russia scandal continued to intensify and shake up American politics.

news.title: 'Dangal' Stages Box Office and Word-of-Mouth Comeback in China
news.body: The Indian film "Dangal" staged a box office comeback in the Chinese market on the strength of rave reviews, breaking the record for an Indian film in China, while Aamir Khan's dedication to his craft sparked widespread discussion.

news.title: China's South China Sea Combustible Ice Test Production Ranks Among World's First
news.body: China's first trial production of natural gas hydrate, or combustible ice, in the Shenhu area of the South China Sea achieved continuous and stable gas output, making the country the first in the world to achieve sustained, stable production in a trial extraction of marine combustible ice.

news.title: Brazilian President Temer Caught Up in Bribery Scandal
news.body: Brazilian media exposed a recording in which President Michel Temer approved hush-money payments to the speaker of the lower house of Congress. News of the recording sent Brazilian stocks plunging nearly 9% and the real tumbling, while calls for Temer to step down swept the country.

news.title: Three Ministries Suspend Campus Lending by Online Lenders
news.body: The China Banking Regulatory Commission, the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security jointly issued a notice on further tightening regulation of campus loans, ordering online lending platforms to suspend all campus lending business and barring them from marketing on campuses without approval.

news.title: Trump Announces US Withdrawal from Paris Agreement
news.body: US President Donald Trump announced that the United States would withdraw from the Paris Agreement, saying the accord harmed the American economy. The move drew global criticism, with China, Europe and other countries reaffirming their commitment to the pact.

news.title: Southern China Hit by Heaviest Rain Since Flood Season Began
news.body: Many parts of southern China experienced the widest-ranging and most intense rainfall since the start of the flood season, with torrential downpours in parts of Jiangxi, Hunan and Fujian, several rivers rising above warning levels, and flood control departments activating emergency responses.

news.title: 'Princess Agents' Premieres to Big Buzz Before Broadcast
news.body: The costume drama "Princess Agents," starring Zhao Liying and Lin Gengxin, was scheduled to premiere on Hunan TV on June 5. The original novel was hugely popular and the trailer passed 100 million views, generating major buzz before the show even aired.

news.title: Ma Long Retains World Championship Men's Singles Title
news.body: The World Table Tennis Championships in Dusseldorf came to a close, with Ma Long edging teammate Fan Zhendong 4-3 in the men's singles final to retain the St. Bride Vase. Ding Ning won the women's singles title as China once again swept multiple crowns.

news.title: Saudi Arabia and Other Countries Cut Ties with Qatar
news.body: Saudi Arabia, Egypt, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and other countries announced they were severing diplomatic relations with Qatar, accusing it of supporting terrorism, triggering a serious diplomatic crisis in the Gulf region.

news.title: National College Entrance Exam Ends as 9.4 Million Students Leave the Halls
news.body: The two-day 2017 national college entrance exam, the gaokao, came to an end, with 9.4 million students across the country sitting the test. Authorities strictly guarded against impersonation and cheating, with facial recognition used to verify identities in many places, and the exam concluded smoothly.

news.title: UK Election Produces Hung Parliament
news.body: Voting in Britain's general election ended, with exit polls showing the ruling Conservative Party losing its majority in the House of Commons and a hung parliament emerging. The prospects for Brexit negotiations grew more uncertain and the pound swung sharply.

news.title: Fuxing Bullet Trains Debut in Both Directions on Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Line
news.body: China's standard Fuxing bullet train made its maiden runs from two stations on the Beijing-Shanghai high-speed railway simultaneously, with test speeds exceeding 400 km/h. With a more elegant shape, longer service life and better safety, it ushered in a new standard era for China's high-speed rail.

news.title: China-India Doklam Standoff Continues as Beijing Lodges Solemn Representations
news.body: Indian border personnel illegally crossed into China's Doklam area and obstructed Chinese road construction, and the standoff between the two militaries continued. China made repeated solemn representations to India demanding the immediate withdrawal of the trespassing personnel.

news.title: Xi Jinping Arrives in Hong Kong for 20th Anniversary Celebrations
news.body: President Xi Jinping arrived in Hong Kong by special plane to attend the meeting celebrating the 20th anniversary of Hong Kong's return to the motherland and the inauguration of the fifth-term government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and to inspect the region.

news.title: 'The Rap of China' Premieres as 'Freestyle' Becomes a Catchphrase
news.body: iQIYI's self-produced online variety show "The Rap of China" quickly became a hit after its premiere, and Kris Wu's line "Do you have freestyle?" flooded the internet, bringing Chinese-language rap culture into the mainstream public eye for the first time.

news.title: North Korea Says It Successfully Test-Fired an ICBM
news.body: North Korea announced it had successfully test-fired a Hwasong-14 intercontinental ballistic missile, with both flight altitude and range reaching new highs. Pyongyang said the missile could strike any corner of the world, the UN Security Council held emergency consultations, and the US and South Korea reacted strongly.

news.title: Persistent Rain in the South Pushes Xiangjiang River Above Record Level
news.body: Sustained heavy rain in southern China pushed the water level at the Changsha station on the Xiangjiang River above its previous record high set in 1998, with severe damage across Hunan. Orange Isle was inundated by floodwaters, and the State Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters upgraded its emergency response to organize rescue and relief work.

news.title: Central Bank Issues Financial Stability Report, Deepening Internet Finance Cleanup
news.body: The People's Bank of China released the China Financial Stability Report (2017), which called for continuing to deepen the special campaign against risks in internet finance and for look-through supervision of peer-to-peer lending, campus loans and other areas, in a bid to prevent and defuse risks in key sectors.

news.title: Hoh Xil Listed as World Heritage Site, China's Largest Natural Heritage Area
news.body: At the 41st session of the World Heritage Committee in Krakow, Poland, Qinghai's Hoh Xil was approved for inscription on the World Natural Heritage List, becoming China's largest world natural heritage site and giving the home of the Tibetan antelope world-class protection.

news.title: Iraq Declares Full Liberation of Mosul
news.body: Iraqi Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi arrived in Mosul and declared the city fully liberated, ending the nearly nine-month battle of Mosul. The extremist group's main stronghold in Iraq was uprooted as the gunsmoke of three years of urban warfare cleared.

news.title: Baidu's Apollo Autonomous Driving Platform Officially Opens
news.body: After Li Yanhong rode in a driverless car onto Beijing's Fifth Ring Road and sparked heated discussion, Baidu fully opened its Apollo autonomous driving platform to developers, saying it would lower the industry's entry barriers and accelerate the commercialization of driverless cars in China.

news.title: Trump Jr. Releases Emails on Meeting with Russian Lawyer
news.body: Donald Trump Jr. released emails about his meeting with a Russian lawyer during last year's election campaign, which showed he knew in advance that she could provide damaging material on Hillary Clinton. The revelation added fresh explosive material to the Russia investigation and shook American politics.

news.title: 'The First Half of My Life' a Hit as Jin Dong and Ma Yili Win Praise
news.body: The urban drama "The First Half of My Life" continued to draw large audiences, with the story of full-time housewife Luo Zijun rebuilding her life in the workplace after a divorce sparking discussion across the internet, while the performances of Jin Dong, Ma Yili and Yuan Quan won wide acclaim.

news.title: Federer Beats Cilic 3-0 at Wimbledon for 19th Grand Slam Title
news.body: In the Wimbledon men's singles final, Federer beat Cilic in straight sets 3-0 to lift the Wimbledon trophy for the eighth time, raising his career Grand Slam singles tally to 19 and adding another chapter to his legend at the age of 35.

news.title: Southern China Enters Scorching Heat Mode as Many Places Top 40°C
news.body: Much of southern China sweltered under sustained heat, with temperatures repeatedly topping 40°C in Shanghai, Hangzhou, Chongqing and elsewhere. Power grids in Jiangsu and Zhejiang repeatedly set record loads, and the National Meteorological Center issued consecutive orange heat alerts.

news.title: Sun Hongbin Elected Chairman of LeTV
news.body: LeTV's board met and elected Sun Hongbin, chairman of Sunac China, as chairman of the third board of directors of LeTV. Jia Yueting, still in the United States, formally stepped aside, and debt-laden LeTV entered the Sun Hongbin era.

news.title: O.J. Simpson Granted Parole and Set for Release
news.body: Nevada's parole board ruled that former football star O.J. Simpson, jailed nine years ago for armed robbery, would be granted parole and could be released as early as October. The "trial of the century" that once gripped the world was back in the headlines.

news.title: Magnitude 7.0 Earthquake Strikes Jiuzhaigou County, Sichuan
news.body: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Jiuzhaigou County in Aba Prefecture, Sichuan, at a depth of 20 kilometers, killing more than 20 people. Tens of thousands of tourists were evacuated and relocated, rescue teams rushed to the area overnight, and the Jiuzhaigou scenic area was temporarily closed.

news.title: US and North Korea Trade Threats as Korean Peninsula Tensions Spike
news.body: Trump warned that North Korea would face "fire and fury like the world has never seen" if it provoked further, and the Korean Central News Agency promptly published a plan to fire missiles toward waters near Guam. The war of words escalated and tensions on the peninsula suddenly ran high.

news.title: Violence in Charlottesville, Virginia, Leaves One Dead
news.body: A white supremacist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia, turned into a violent clash, and a man drove his car into a crowd of counter-protesters, killing one person and injuring many others. Trump's statement blaming violence on both sides drew widespread criticism.

news.title: 'Wolf Warrior 2' Tops Chinese Film History with 3.8 Billion Yuan
news.body: The military action blockbuster "Wolf Warrior 2," directed by and starring Wu Jing, passed 3.8 billion yuan in cumulative box office, overtaking "The Mermaid" to top the all-time Chinese film chart, as the viewing frenzy and patriotic debate it stirred swept the country.

news.title: Banking Regulator Issues Disclosure Guidelines for Online Lending
news.body: The China Banking Regulatory Commission issued guidelines on information disclosure for online lending intermediaries, requiring platforms to promptly disclose key information such as matched transaction volumes, borrowers and overdue and compensatory payments, in order to protect lenders' right to know.

news.title: Typhoon Hato Slams Pearl River Estuary, Devastating Zhuhai and Macau
news.body: Typhoon Hato, the strongest storm of the year, made landfall in Zhuhai at severe typhoon intensity, bringing fierce winds, torrential rain and towering waves to the Pearl River Estuary. Zhuhai and Macau were badly hit, work and school were suspended in many parts of the Greater Bay Area, and city life gradually returned to order after the storm passed.

news.title: Indian Guru Convicted of Rape, Triggering Massive Riots
news.body: Indian guru Ram Rahim Singh was convicted of rape and sentenced to 20 years in prison, and his followers launched large-scale riots in Haryana, Punjab and elsewhere, leaving dozens dead and prompting troops and police to impose curfews in several cities.

news.title: Haidilao Kitchen Hygiene Scandal Exposed as Chain Responds Quickly
news.body: "Legal Evening News" published an undercover investigation showing rats running through the kitchens of Haidilao's Jinsong and Taiyanggong outlets in Beijing and a ladle used to clear a drain, among other problems. Haidilao issued a statement admitting the issues and apologizing, and its "we'll take the blame" crisis response sparked wide discussion.

news.title: Mayweather Stops McGregor in Round 10 to Retire at 50-0
news.body: The "fight of the century" took place in Las Vegas, where UFC star Conor McGregor crossed over to challenge unbeaten boxing champion Floyd Mayweather. Mayweather won by TKO in the 10th round, retiring from the professional ring with a perfect 50-0 record as the two split hundreds of millions of dollars in purse money.

news.title: North Korean Missile Flies Over Japan, Raising Tensions Again
news.body: North Korea fired a Hwasong-12 ballistic missile that flew over Hokkaido before falling into the Pacific Ocean. Japan activated its nationwide instantaneous alert system, Prime Minister Shinzo Abe convened an emergency national security meeting, and the United States, Japan and South Korea strongly condemned the launch.

news.title: Hurricane Harvey Devastates Texas as Houston Is Swamped
news.body: Category 4 Hurricane Harvey made landfall on the Texas coast and stalled for days, bringing historic and catastrophic flooding to Houston that killed dozens. The heart of America's oil refining industry was paralyzed for a time, and oil prices swung in response.

news.title: Huawei Unveils Kirin 970, World's First Phone AI Chip
news.body: Huawei unveiled its Kirin 970 chip ahead of the IFA show in Berlin. The first chip to integrate a dedicated neural network processing unit, it became the world's first smartphone AI chip, opening the era of on-device artificial intelligence.

news.title: China Beats Qatar 2-1 in Final World Cup Qualifier
news.body: In the last round of the Asian qualifiers for the 2018 World Cup, China, reduced to ten men, came from 1-0 down in Doha to score twice and beat Qatar 2-1, with Xiao Zhi and Wu Lei finding the net. Although an inferior points record kept China out of the playoff, the team won its honor match and bowed out with heads high.

news.title: North Korea's Sixth Nuclear Test Draws Strong International Reaction
news.body: North Korea announced it had successfully tested a hydrogen bomb that could be mounted on an intercontinental missile, and South Korea's weather agency detected an artificial earthquake. The UN Security Council began consultations on a new round of sanctions as the international community strongly condemned the North's sixth nuclear test.

news.title: Hurricane Irma Lashes the Caribbean and Closes In on Florida
news.body: Category 5 Hurricane Irma tore through Caribbean islands and barreled toward the US state of Florida, prompting the emergency evacuation of millions of people there. Miami was on high alert, and several Caribbean islands suffered devastating damage.

news.title: Magnitude 8.2 Quake Off Mexico, Strongest in a Century
news.body: A magnitude 8.2 earthquake struck off the coast of Chiapas, Mexico, the strongest quake to hit the country in more than a hundred years, killing nearly 100 people. Several countries along the Pacific coast issued tsunami warnings.

news.title: Magnitude 7.1 Quake Shakes Mexico City, Toppling Hundreds of Buildings
news.body: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck central Mexico with an epicenter about 120 kilometers from Mexico City, on the 32nd anniversary of the devastating 1985 quake. Hundreds of buildings collapsed and more than 300 people died as the entire city mounted a desperate rescue effort.

news.title: National Cybersecurity Week Focuses on Building Security Together
news.body: The 2017 National Cybersecurity Week opened in Shanghai under the theme "cybersecurity for the people, cybersecurity by the people," showcasing the latest achievements in cybersecurity technology and opening a range of interactive experiences to the public.

news.title: Fed Announces Balance Sheet Runoff to Begin in October
news.body: The Federal Reserve ended its policy meeting by leaving interest rates unchanged and announcing that it would begin shrinking its balance sheet in October, the first runoff in nearly a decade since the financial crisis, with one more rate hike still possible this year.

news.title: Li Chen's Proposal to Fan Bingbing Caps Four Years of Romance
news.body: Li Chen got down on one knee at Fan Bingbing's 36th birthday party and successfully proposed, moving her to tears. After four years together the couple finally got engaged, and Weibo lit up as half the entertainment industry sent congratulations.

news.title: iPhone 8 Launch Fails to Excite in China as Fans Wait for iPhone X
news.body: The iPhone 8 and 8 Plus went on sale officially, but were criticized for the limited upgrades, described as squeezing out the toothpaste. Queues at Apple stores in many cities on launch day were noticeably shorter than in previous years, with many Apple fans holding their money for the full-screen flagship iPhone X.

news.title: Eight-Day Super Golden Week Ahead as Holiday Trips Seen Topping 600 Million
news.body: The eight-day super Golden Week created by the overlap of National Day and the Mid-Autumn Festival was in the final countdown, with travel agencies predicting more than 600 million trips. Bookings for overseas travel, self-driving trips and high-speed rail tours were hot, with tickets hard to come by on some popular routes.

news.title: Merkel Wins Fourth Term in German Election
news.body: Results of Germany's Bundestag election showed Merkel's CDU/CSU bloc remaining the largest party, giving her a fourth term as chancellor. The far-right Alternative for Germany entered parliament for the first time, and coalition talks began with difficulty.

news.title: Mahua FunAge's 'Never Say Die' Ignites National Day Holiday Box Office
news.body: The Mahua FunAge comedy "Never Say Die" opened, with Allen and Ma Li playing boxers whose bodies are swapped in a laugh-out-loud story. Advance screenings drew rave reviews, first-day box office passed 100 million yuan, and the film led the National Day holiday slate.

news.title: Las Vegas Shooting Kills 59, Deadliest in Modern US History
news.body: A gunman opened fire on a crowd at a country music festival in Las Vegas from the 32nd floor of the Mandalay Bay hotel, killing 59 people and wounding more than 500, making it the deadliest mass shooting in modern American history.

news.title: Super Golden Week Opens with Over 110 Million Tourist Trips Nationwide
news.body: On the first day of the eight-day super Golden Week combining National Day and the Mid-Autumn Festival, China received 113 million tourist visits nationwide, rail passenger numbers topped ten million for consecutive days, and revolutionary heritage tours, self-driving trips and rural tourism stayed red hot.

news.title: Kazuo Ishiguro Wins 2017 Nobel Prize in Literature
news.body: The 2017 Nobel Prize in Literature went to Japanese-born British author Kazuo Ishiguro. His best-known works, "The Remains of the Day" and "Never Let Me Go," explore memory, time and self-deception in delicate, restrained prose, and the surprise win sent book lovers worldwide rushing to buy his books.

news.title: 460 Million Holiday Trips in First Four Days of Golden Week
news.body: In the first four days of the National Day and Mid-Autumn holiday, China received a total of 461 million tourist visits and generated 385.6 billion yuan in tourism revenue. Popular scenic spots stayed packed, and traveling off-peak became a new choice for many visitors.

news.title: US Announces Withdrawal from UNESCO
news.body: The US State Department announced that the United States would withdraw from UNESCO, citing a steadily worsening arrears problem and the organization's bias against Israel. Israel then announced it would follow suit, drawing deep regret from the international community.

news.title: Lu Han's Relationship Announcement Crashes Weibo
news.body: Lu Han suddenly made his relationship with Guan Xiaotong public on Weibo, and the announcement post instantly detonated the internet, briefly crashing Sina Weibo. Fans were heartbroken and onlookers gossiped as related topics topped the trending charts for days.

news.title: Regulators in Several Cities Screen Cash-Loan Platforms as Crackdown Looms
news.body: Financial regulators in Shanghai, Beijing and other places began screening and surveying cash-loan platforms, and regulators conducted intensive research toward drafting cash-loan rules. Expectations of a crackdown on high interest rates, aggressive debt collection and up-front fee deductions suddenly intensified.

news.title: Abe's Bloc Wins Big in Japan's Lower House Election, Pro-Revision Forces Pass Two-Thirds
news.body: Japan's 48th House of Representatives election was held and counted, with the ruling LDP-Komeito coalition winning big and taking more than two-thirds of the seats. Shinzo Abe will stay in power, clearing the seat threshold needed to revise the constitution.

news.title: iPhone X Pre-Orders Crash Apple's Website Worldwide
news.body: iPhone X pre-orders opened worldwide, and the Face ID and full-screen design set off a buying frenzy. Apple's website was briefly overwhelmed, the first batch of stock sold out within minutes, shipping times generally stretched to five to six weeks, and scalpers charged staggering markups.

news.title: Catalonia Declares Independence Unilaterally as Spain Moves to Take Over
news.body: Catalonia's regional parliament voted to declare independence unilaterally, and Spain's Senate immediately authorized the central government to invoke Article 155 to take over the region. Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy dissolved the regional government and called fresh elections as large protests erupted in Barcelona.

news.title: Truck Attack Near World Trade Center in Manhattan Kills 8
news.body: A truck rammed into pedestrians near the World Trade Center in Lower Manhattan, New York, in an attack that also involved gunfire, killing 8 people and injuring more than a dozen. The 29-year-old suspect was shot and wounded by police before being captured. The United States classified the attack as terrorism and investigated possible extremist links.

news.title: Nationwide Drive to Study and Implement Party Congress Spirit
news.body: After the successful conclusion of the 19th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, departments and localities across the country quickly launched a drive to study, publicize and implement the congress's spirit, unifying thinking around it and pooling strength to accomplish the tasks it set out.

news.title: Church Shooting in Small Texas Town Kills 26
news.body: A gunman opened fire at a church in Sutherland Springs, Texas, killing 26 people and wounding more than 20, the youngest victim just 18 months old. The shooter's motive was linked to a family dispute, and the debate over gun control heated up again.

news.title: First Two BeiDou-3 Satellites Launched Successfully
news.body: China successfully launched the first two BeiDou-3 satellites for its global navigation network aboard a single rocket from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center, marking the formal start of the global constellation build-out for the BeiDou satellite navigation system as China's system accelerates its push into the world.

news.title: Saudi Arabia Launches Unprecedented Anti-Corruption Sweep
news.body: Saudi Arabia set up a supreme anti-corruption committee and arrested dozens of princes and current and former cabinet ministers overnight, including the world's richest man, Prince Alwaleed bin Talal. Public opinion widely held that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was using the crackdown to further consolidate power.

news.title: Acting Talent Show 'The Birth of an Actor' Sparks National Debate
news.body: Zhejiang Television's variety show "The Birth of an Actor" became a hit, with mentors Zhang Ziyi and Song Dandan clashing fiercely over acting skill versus star power, while the performances of young actors such as Zheng Shuang and Ouyang Nana triggered a nationwide debate about acting.

news.title: Trump Arrives in Beijing as China and US Sign $250 Billion in Deals
news.body: US President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing for his first visit to China since taking office. Chinese and US companies signed business deals worth a total of $253.5 billion, and tea at the Palace Museum's Baoyun Building became a diplomatic highlight.

news.title: Tencent Market Value Passes Facebook to Enter Global Top Five
news.body: Tencent's share price kept climbing, and its market value overtook Facebook's to make it the fifth most valuable company in the world, alongside Apple, Google's parent company, Microsoft and Amazon, confirming the global standing of China's technology giants.

news.title: Sogou Lists on NYSE as Wang Xiaochuan Rings the Bell with His Mother
news.body: Sogou officially listed on the New York Stock Exchange, opening at $13 a share. CEO Wang Xiaochuan rang the opening bell together with his mother. With Tencent as its largest shareholder, the company pitched its AI story around the twin engines of search and input methods.

news.title: Tmall Double 11 Gala Kicks Off a Star-Studded Night of Shopping
news.body: The 2017 Tmall Double 11 Global Shopping Festival gala was held in grand style, with stars including Zhang Ziyi, Kris Wu and Li Yuchun taking the stage. When the clock struck midnight, the nationwide shopping frenzy officially began and transaction figures across platforms kept breaking records.

news.title: Shenhua Beats SIPG 1-0 in First Leg of FA Cup Final
news.body: The first leg of the 2017 Chinese FA Cup final, a Shanghai derby, kicked off at Hongkou Football Stadium. Martins scored in the second half as Shanghai Greenland Shenhua beat Shanghai SIPG 1-0 at home to seize the upper hand in the two-legged final.

news.title: Zimbabwe's Political Upheaval Ends Mugabe's Rule
news.body: After Zimbabwe's military took over power, 93-year-old President Robert Mugabe, who had ruled the country for 37 years, announced his resignation under impeachment pressure from parliament. Former vice president Emmerson Mnangagwa was sworn in as the new president, closing an era.

news.title: New Cash-Loan Rules Out for Comment as Online Micro-Lending Licenses Halted
news.body: The office leading the special campaign against risks in internet finance issued an urgent notice ordering all localities to suspend approval of online micro-lending companies. A draft notice on regulating and rectifying cash-loan business then circulated, with an interest rate ceiling and lending qualification requirements on the way, sending shockwaves through the industry.

news.title: Beijing Police Report Findings in RYB Kindergarten Case
news.body: Beijing police reported the findings of their investigation into the RYB New World Kindergarten case. Teacher Liu Yanan was criminally detained on suspicion of abusing a person in her care, while those who fabricated rumors about a "tiger group" punishment were dealt with according to law. RYB Education's share price had plunged the previous day, and the company publicly apologized and promised reforms.

news.title: Wave of Bike-Sharing Bankruptcies Sounds Deposit Alarm
news.body: Bluegogo, Kuke Bike and others went under one after another, leaving tens of millions of users unable to get their deposits back. The bike-sharing industry fell from frenzied expansion into a freezing winter of consolidation, and the difficulty of regulating deposits drew nationwide attention.

news.title: Iraq Declares Final Victory over Extremist Group
news.body: Iraqi Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi declared that after more than three years of fighting, Iraq had completely defeated the extremist group on its territory and won the final victory in its war on terror, though the road to reconstruction and reconciliation remained long.

news.title: National Memorial Ceremony Held for Nanjing Massacre Victims
news.body: The fourth national memorial ceremony for the victims of the Nanjing Massacre was held at the Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders. Sirens sounded across Nanjing as representatives from all walks of life mourned the 300,000 victims, with the past recalled as a warning to those who came after.

news.title: Fed Raises Rates a Quarter Point for Third Time This Year
news.body: The Federal Reserve announced a quarter-point rate increase to a range of 1.25% to 1.5%, its third hike of the year, and projected three more increases in 2018. The final policy meeting before Janet Yellen steps down kept global markets on edge.

news.title: Document No. 57 Sets Clear Deadline for P2P Rectification
news.body: The office of the leading group for the special campaign against risks in P2P online lending issued a notice to localities on completing rectification and acceptance checks for P2P lending risks, requiring each region to finish checks on major online lending institutions by the end of April 2018 and all of them by the end of June, with those failing the checks guided into an orderly wind-down or shut down.

news.title: Feng Xiaogang's 'Youth' Opens to Rave Reviews
news.body: Feng Xiaogang's coming-of-age drama "Youth" opened officially, and its portrayal of the youth and fate of a 1970s military song-and-dance troupe moved countless viewers to tears. Box office passed 300 million yuan in its first weekend as the year-end holiday season got under way.

news.title: Real Madrid Beats Gremio 1-0 to Win Club World Cup and Fifth Trophy of the Year
news.body: In the FIFA Club World Cup final in Abu Dhabi, Real Madrid beat Brazil's Gremio 1-0 through a second-half Ronaldo free kick, successfully defending the title and crowning a year in which the club won five trophies.

news.title: Tokyo Court Jails Jiang Ge's Killer Chen Shifeng for 20 Years
news.body: The Tokyo District Court handed down a first-instance verdict in the case of Chinese student Jiang Ge, who was murdered in Japan, sentencing her killer Chen Shifeng to 20 years in prison. The case, which took more than a year, sparked lasting debate about human nature, friendship and the law.

news.title: Security Council Unanimously Adopts New Sanctions on North Korea
news.body: The UN Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2397 imposing a new round of sanctions on North Korea, cutting its annual ceiling for imports of refined petroleum products by half and requiring North Korean overseas workers to return home within a set period. Pyongyang protested strongly.

news.title: Chen Kaige's 'Legend of the Demon Cat' Dazzles with Tang Aesthetics
news.body: Chen Kaige's fantasy blockbuster "Legend of the Demon Cat" opened, with Huang Xuan and Shota Sometani joining forces to investigate a strange case in the heyday of the Tang dynasty. The spectacular Tang aesthetics of the Feast of Ultimate Bliss dazzled audiences as competition in the year-end season intensified.

news.title: WeChat's 'Jump Jump' Mini Game Floods Social Feeds
news.body: WeChat released a new version officially introducing mini games, and its flagship game "Jump Jump" flooded social feeds overnight, with young and old alike tapping away at their screens. The mini game ecosystem and the value of WeChat's traffic gateway sparked heated industry discussion.

news.title: 'The Ex-File 3' Opens, Setting Up a Year-End Dark Horse Run
news.body: The romantic comedy "The Ex-File 3: The Return of the Exes," starring Zheng Kai and Han Geng, opened, aiming at the New Year holiday slot. The modestly budgeted film went on to stage a strong comeback on the strength of intense emotional resonance, becoming the biggest dark horse of the year-end season.

news.title: Kim Jong Un Delivers New Year's Address
news.body: North Korea's supreme leader Kim Jong Un delivered a New Year's address, saying North Korea was willing to send a delegation to the Pyeongchang Winter Olympics and was open to talks with South Korea on the matter, signs of a thaw in tensions on the Korean Peninsula.

news.title: Cities Across China Welcome First Day of 2018
news.body: Residents of major cities across the country welcomed the new year with flag-raising ceremonies, fun runs and other events. Large crowds gathered for New Year's Eve celebrations in places such as Shijingshan in Beijing and the Bund in Shanghai, and public order remained stable.

news.title: Hefei Subway Fare Evader Detained by Police
news.body: A man in Hefei repeatedly jumped the turnstiles to evade subway fares and insulted staff, and was administratively detained by police, the first case in the city of detention for subway fare evasion.

news.title: China Successfully Launches SuperView-1 Microwave Satellite Constellation
news.body: China successfully launched the SuperView-1 microwave satellite constellation into space aboard a Long March 2D rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, and the satellites entered their planned orbits.

news.title: US and North Korea Comment on Inter-Korean High-Level Talks
news.body: The White House said US President Donald Trump welcomed the reopening of the inter-Korean liaison channel at Panmunjom, and the two Koreas agreed to hold high-level talks on the South Korean side of Panmunjom on the 9th.

news.title: Lanzhou and Hefei Property Policy Loosening Draws Attention
news.body: Lanzhou scrapped home purchase restrictions in some districts, and Hefei was reported to be easing price caps. Both cities said the moves were targeted fine-tuning, sparking nationwide discussion about the direction of property policy.

news.title: Five Arrested in Ctrip Daycare Child Abuse Case
news.body: Investigations into the child abuse case at a Ctrip-affiliated daycare center in Shanghai made progress, with the procuratorate approving the arrest of five staff members involved and the case entering judicial proceedings.

news.title: Inter-Korean High-Level Talks Held at Panmunjom
news.body: North and South Korea held high-level talks on the South Korean side of Panmunjom, agreeing that the North would send a delegation to the Pyeongchang Winter Olympics and that the two sides would hold talks between their military authorities.

news.title: Wozniacki Beats Mertens 2-1 to Reach Australian Open Final
news.body: In the women's singles semifinal at the Australian Open, Denmark's Caroline Wozniacki beat Belgium's Elise Mertens 2-1 to reach the final and take aim at the world number one ranking.

news.title: World Economic Forum Annual Meeting 2018 Opens in Davos
news.body: The World Economic Forum's 2018 annual meeting opened in Davos, Switzerland. US President Donald Trump was to attend and speak, under the theme "Creating a Shared Future in a Fractured World."

news.title: Geely Satellite Project Breaks Ground in Taizhou
news.body: Geely Group's satellite project, with total investment of several billion yuan, broke ground in Taizhou, laying out low-orbit satellites and connected vehicles and pioneering commercial space for a Chinese automaker.

news.title: Findings Released in Snow Town Tourist Gouging Case
news.body: The findings of the investigation into the gouging of tourists at the "Zhao Family Courtyard" in Snow Town, Heilongjiang, were released. The family inn involved was fined and ordered to suspend operations for rectification, and local authorities promised to rebuild the area's tourism image.

news.title: Spring Festival Travel Rush of 2018 Officially Begins
news.body: The 40-day Spring Festival travel rush got under way, with about 2.98 billion passenger trips expected nationwide. High-speed rail and ride-hailing became new choices for heading home.

news.title: British Prime Minister Theresa May Visits China
