news.body: British Prime Minister Theresa May arrived in Wuhan to begin her visit to China, and China and Britain signed business cooperation agreements worth about 9 billion pounds, covering areas including the Belt and Road Initiative.

news.title: China Launches Electromagnetic Monitoring Satellite Zhangheng-1
news.body: China successfully launched the Zhangheng-1 electromagnetic monitoring test satellite into space aboard a Long March 2D rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, for use in earthquake monitoring and early warning research.

news.title: Hunan TV Records Spring Festival Gala for Little New Year
news.body: Hunan TV finished recording its 2018 Little New Year Spring Festival gala, with hosts including He Jiong and Xie Na appearing alongside a lineup of stars. It was to air on the evening of Little New Year.

news.title: Baihang Credit Licensed for Personal Credit Reporting
news.body: The People's Bank of China published details of the preparations for Baihang Credit Co., whose main shareholders are the National Internet Finance Association of China and eight institutions including Sesame Credit and Tencent Credit. China's first personal credit reporting license went to Baihang Credit, breaking the impasse over a unified credit reporting body.

news.title: Dow Plunges 1,000 Points Intraday
news.body: US stocks fell sharply for consecutive sessions, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropping nearly 1,600 points at one point, a record intraday fall. Global markets were shaken, raising concerns about the US bull market.

news.title: Police Dismiss Reports of J-20 Pilot's Death
news.body: In response to rumors circulating online that a J-20 pilot had been killed, police refuted the claims as false and said those who spread the rumors had been dealt with according to law.

news.title: Global Markets Continue to Swing
news.body: Global stock markets continued to swing after a "black week," with major Asian indexes mixed as investors focused on US inflation data and the pace of interest rate hikes.

news.title: Public Security Ministry Rolls Out Spring Festival Convenience Measures
news.body: The Ministry of Public Security introduced a series of convenience measures for the Spring Festival, including extended vehicle management office hours during the holiday and handling of traffic violations committed in other jurisdictions, making it easier for the public to get things done during the holiday.

news.title: Florida School Shooting Leaves 17 Dead
news.body: A shooting at a high school in Parkland, Florida, killed 17 people and wounded many others, and a 19-year-old gunman was arrested. The attack set off another nationwide debate about gun control in the United States.

news.title: Wu Dajing Wins 500m Short Track Gold in Pyeongchang
news.body: In the men's 500m short track speed skating final at the Pyeongchang Winter Olympics, China's Wu Dajing won gold in 39.584 seconds, setting a new world record and giving China its first gold medal of these Games.

news.title: Return Travel Peaks as Spring Festival Holiday Nears End
news.body: As the Spring Festival holiday drew to a close, railways nationwide saw a peak in return travel, with passenger numbers climbing steadily from the fourth day of the first lunar month and extra trains added in many places.

news.title: Trump Announces Heavy Tariffs on Steel and Aluminum
news.body: US President Donald Trump announced tariffs of 25% on imported steel and 10% on imported aluminum, drawing strong reactions from major trading partners including the European Union and China.

news.title: Personal Income Tax Threshold to Rise Under Budget Plan
news.body: Premier Li Keqiang said in the government work report that China would raise the personal income tax threshold in 2018 and add special deductions for expenses such as children's education and major medical bills.

news.title: First Session of 13th National People's Congress Opens in Beijing
news.body: The first session of the 13th National People's Congress opened at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, with nearly 3,000 deputies attending to hear the government work report.

news.title: Film 'Operation Red Sea' Stages Box Office Comeback
news.body: The Spring Festival release "Operation Red Sea" staged a box office comeback on the strength of word of mouth, with cumulative ticket sales passing 3 billion yuan and the film ranking near the top of China's all-time box office chart.

news.title: NPC Session Elects New State Leaders
news.body: The first session of the 13th National People's Congress held its fifth plenary meeting and elected a new group of state leaders, with Xi Jinping elected unanimously as President of the People's Republic of China and Chairman of the Central Military Commission of the People's Republic of China.

news.title: 3·15 Gala Exposes Volkswagen Touareg Engine Water Ingress and Other Problems
news.body: CCTV's 3·15 consumer rights gala exposed problems including engine water ingress in imported Volkswagen Touareg vehicles and the difficulty of getting bike-sharing deposits refunded, and the companies involved apologized overnight.

news.title: First Session of 13th National People's Congress Concludes
news.body: The first session of the 13th National People's Congress concluded successfully in Beijing, adopting the government work report and the supervision law, among other items, and completing all items on its agenda.

news.title: Central Bank Cuts Reserve Requirements to Support Inclusive Finance
news.body: The People's Bank of China cut reserve requirements in a targeted move to support inclusive finance, releasing about 450 billion yuan in long-term funds to help financial institutions serve small and micro enterprises and other sectors.

news.title: Ding Junhui Beats O'Sullivan 10-3 to Win Players Championship
news.body: In the final of the snooker Players Championship, China's Ding Junhui swept Ronnie O'Sullivan 10-3 to take the title, ending years without a win over "The Rocket" and claiming his 14th ranking event crown.

news.title: Former South Korean President Lee Myung-bak Questioned by Prosecutors
news.body: Former South Korean president Lee Myung-bak was summoned and questioned by prosecutors over bribery and other allegations, making him the second former president to be investigated after Park Geun-hye.

news.title: China Successfully Launches Gaofen-1 02 and 03 Satellites
news.body: China successfully launched the Gaofen-1 02 and 03 satellites into space aboard a Long March 4C rocket from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, and the satellites entered their planned orbits.

news.title: Results Released in Xi'an Home Lottery Rigging Case
news.body: The results of the investigation into rigged lottery allocations at the South Chang'an Street No. 1 property project in Xi'an were released, with 35 public officials held accountable and the company involved penalized.

news.title: Liaoning Sweeps Guangsha 4-0 for First CBA Title
news.body: In Game 4 of the CBA Finals, the Liaoning men's team beat Zhejiang Guangsha 100-88 at home to complete a 4-0 series sweep and claim the first CBA championship in franchise history.

news.title: New Rules on Flight Delay Compensation Open for Public Comment
news.body: Implementation rules attached to the Regulations on the Normal Operation of Flights have been released for public comment, setting out clearer provisions on notifying passengers of delays and on compensation standards.

news.title: US Sanctions ZTE
news.body: The US Commerce Department announced an export ban on China's ZTE, barring American companies from selling components to the firm for seven years; trading in both ZTE's A-shares and H-shares was suspended, setting off a nationwide debate in China about self-reliance in the chip industry.

news.title: Master Plan for Xiongan New Area in Hebei Released
news.body: The Master Plan for the Xiongan New Area in Hebei was officially released, defining the area's scope, spatial layout and development goals, and marking a new stage in the construction of the new district.

news.title: US, UK and France Launch Airstrikes on Syria
news.body: Citing a "chemical weapons attack" in Syria, the United States, Britain and France carried out military strikes on targets inside the country; the Syrian military said it intercepted most of the missiles, and the UN Security Council held emergency consultations.

news.title: National Conference on Cybersecurity and IT Application Convened
news.body: A national conference on cybersecurity and IT application was held in Beijing, stressing the need to seize the historic opportunities of the information age and to build China into a cyber power through independent innovation.

news.title: First Digital China Summit Opens in Fuzhou
news.body: The first Digital China Summit opened in Fuzhou, Fujian, showcasing China's achievements in e-government and the digital economy, with academicians of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the Chinese Academy of Engineering and corporate leaders in attendance.

news.title: 'Us and Them' Sets First-Day Box Office Record
news.body: The film Us and Them, directed by Rene Liu, took more than 280 million yuan on its opening day, a new record for a romance film, before becoming mired in a controversy over refunded tickets.

news.title: Law on Protecting Heroes and Martyrs Passed Unanimously
news.body: The second session of the Standing Committee of the 13th National People's Congress unanimously passed the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Heroes and Martyrs, enshrining the dignity of heroes and martyrs in law; it took effect on May 1.

news.title: Final Preparations Under Way for North-South Korea Summit
news.body: North and South Korea made last-minute preparations for their third summit, with the Peace House on the South Korean side of Panmunjom ready for the meeting, which drew global attention.

news.title: May Day Holiday Tourism Booms Nationwide
news.body: During the May Day holiday, China received 147 million domestic tourist visits and generated 87.16 billion yuan in domestic tourism revenue, with red tourism and rural tourism proving popular choices.

news.title: Inter-Korean Summit Held
news.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and South Korean President Moon Jae-in met at Panmunjom and signed the Panmunjom Declaration, pledging to halt hostile acts and marking a major turning point on the Korean Peninsula.

news.title: Several Cities Adjust Mortgage Rates
news.body: Beijing, Guangzhou, Shenzhen and several other cities raised interest rates on first-home mortgages, with some banks applying a 15 percent premium over the benchmark rate as property market controls stayed tight.

news.title: US Pulls Back From the Eye of the Israeli-Palestinian Storm
news.body: The relocation of the US embassy in Israel to Jerusalem triggered large-scale clashes in the Gaza Strip that left dozens of Palestinians dead, and the United Nations called for an independent investigation.

news.title: Conference Marking 200th Anniversary of Marx's Birth Held
news.body: A conference marking the 200th anniversary of Karl Marx's birth was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, where it was stressed that Marxism is the soul of the ideals and convictions of Chinese Communists.

news.title: 'Avengers: Infinity War' Takes Over 400 Million Yuan on Opening Day on the Mainland
news.body: The Hollywood blockbuster Avengers: Infinity War opened in mainland China, grossing more than 400 million yuan on its first day and setting several box office records.

news.title: Mahathir Wins Malaysia's General Election
news.body: Malaysia held a general election in which the opposition alliance led by 92-year-old former prime minister Mahathir Mohamad won, ending more than 60 years in power for the ruling Barisan Nasional coalition and returning Mahathir to the premiership.

news.title: China Successfully Launches Gaofen-5 Satellite
news.body: China successfully launched the Gaofen-5 satellite aboard a Long March 4C rocket from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center; the satellite can carry out hyperspectral observation of atmospheric pollutants and other targets.

news.title: Second Batch of Mixed-Ownership Reform Pilots Expanded
news.body: The National Development and Reform Commission said the pilot programme for mixed-ownership reform has been expanded to more than 100 enterprises, with substantive steps to follow in the power, oil, natural gas and railway sectors.

news.title: US Embassy in Jerusalem Opens
news.body: The US embassy in Israel officially opened in Jerusalem, drawing widespread international controversy as fierce clashes between Israelis and Palestinians in the Gaza Strip left many dead and wounded.

news.title: Real Madrid Beats Liverpool 3-1 in Champions League Final for Third Straight Title
news.body: In the Champions League final in Kiev, Real Madrid beat Liverpool 3-1 with two goals from Gareth Bale to win a third consecutive European title, with Cristiano Ronaldo and other stars reaching the summit of European football.

news.title: China Issues First Cybersecurity Enforcement Standard
news.body: The Ministry of Public Security released a draft regulation on multi-level protection of cybersecurity, taking the system into the 2.0 era with broader regulatory coverage.

news.title: China Successfully Launches Gaofen-6 Satellite
news.body: China successfully launched the Gaofen-6 satellite aboard a Long March 2D rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center; the satellite will operate in a network with Gaofen-1 to serve agriculture, rural development and disaster monitoring.

news.title: Draft Amendment to Individual Income Tax Law Opens for Public Comment
news.body: A draft amendment to the Individual Income Tax Law was published for public comment, proposing to raise the monthly tax threshold from 3,500 yuan to 5,000 yuan, sparking heated nationwide discussion.

news.title: Gaokao Approaches in 2018 as Localities Step Up Support
news.body: China's national college entrance exam, the gaokao, was about to begin, with 9.75 million candidates set to enter examination halls, a new high in recent years, as localities rolled out support measures such as free rides to test centres and noise control.

news.title: Palestinian Militant Groups and Israel Reach Brief Ceasefire
news.body: With mediation from the United Nations and Egypt, armed groups in the Gaza Strip and Israel reached a brief ceasefire, temporarily halting days of rocket fire and airstrikes.

news.title: Kim Jong Un and Trump Meet in Singapore
news.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and US President Donald Trump held their first meeting in Singapore and signed a joint statement reaching consensus on issues including the denuclearisation of the Korean Peninsula, the first-ever historic meeting between a sitting US president and a North Korean leader.

news.title: SCO Qingdao Summit Closes
news.body: The 18th meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation closed in Qingdao with the adoption of the Qingdao Declaration; Xi Jinping chaired the meeting and delivered a speech, and the first summit after the SCO's expansion produced substantial results.

news.title: 2018 Gaokao Results Released Across the Country
news.body: Gaokao results were released province by province, with candidates able to check their scores through official channels; many places offered big-data services to help with application choices, and warnings against diploma mill scams flooded social media.

news.title: US Announces Withdrawal From UN Human Rights Council
news.body: The United States announced its withdrawal from the UN Human Rights Council, saying the body harbours political bias; the United Nations expressed regret over the decision.

news.title: Individual Income Tax Threshold of 5,000 Yuan Submitted for Deliberation
news.body: A draft amendment to the Individual Income Tax Law was submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for deliberation, proposing to raise the threshold to 60,000 yuan a year and to introduce special additional deductions, benefiting wage earners broadly.

news.title: 'How Long Will I Love U' Wins Praise and Box Office
news.body: The film How Long Will I Love U, starring Lei Jiayin and Tong Liya, passed 900 million yuan in cumulative box office, emerging as a dark horse of its release window, while director Su Lun won acclaim with her feature debut.

news.title: Russia Rout Saudi Arabia 5-0 in World Cup Opener
news.body: The 2018 World Cup opened at Moscow's Luzhniki Stadium, where hosts Russia thrashed Saudi Arabia 5-0 and Yuri Gazinsky headed in the first goal of the tournament.

news.title: First National Pollution Source Census Bulletin Released
news.body: The State Council Information Office released the Second National Pollution Source Census Bulletin, which provides a comprehensive picture of pollution sources of all kinds and data support for precision pollution control.

news.title: Erdogan Re-elected in Turkey's Election
news.body: Turkey held presidential and parliamentary elections in which incumbent President Recep Tayyip Erdogan won in the first round to secure another term, as the country formally moved to a presidential system of government.

news.title: China's Homegrown AG600 Large Aircraft Completes First Water Takeoff and Landing
news.body: The AG600, a large amphibious aircraft developed independently by China, successfully completed its first takeoff and landing on water in Jingmen, Hubei, making it the largest amphibious aircraft under development in the world.

news.title: 2018 Railway Summer Travel Season Begins
news.body: The national railway summer travel season officially began, with 650 million passenger trips expected in July and August; student and tourist travel overlapped and services were stepped up on several high-speed rail lines.

news.title: Mexico's Election Shakes Up Latin American Politics
news.body: Mexico held a presidential election in which left-wing candidate Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador won by a landslide, becoming the country's first leftist president in decades, with leaders from many countries offering congratulations.

news.title: Thailand Races to Rescue Boys Trapped in Cave
news.body: Twelve members of a youth football team and their coach were trapped for days in a cave in Chiang Rai, Thailand; international rescue teams gathered and began moving the group out in batches from the evening of July 8, in an operation that gripped the world.

news.title: Next Phase of Special Campaign Against Internet Finance Risks Mapped Out
news.body: The People's Bank of China met with the leading group for the special campaign against internet finance risks to set out the next phase of the work, stressing that risk disposal in online lending and other areas should follow the overall requirements for forestalling and defusing major risks.

news.title: France Beats Croatia 4-2 to Win 2018 World Cup
news.body: The 2018 World Cup final at Moscow's Luzhniki Stadium saw France beat Croatia 4-2 to lift the trophy again after 20 years, with Kylian Mbappe named best young player.

news.title: China Successfully Launches Two Pakistani Satellites
news.body: China successfully launched two satellites, including Pakistan's Remote Sensing Satellite-1, aboard a single Long March 3B rocket from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center.

news.title: Changchun Changsheng Vaccine Scandal Sparks Public Outcry
news.body: The National Medical Products Administration reported that Changchun Changsheng had falsified production records for its rabies vaccine, drawing nationwide concern over the problem vaccines; the State Council dispatched an investigation team to Jilin overnight for a full inquiry.

news.title: NATO Summit Held in Brussels
news.body: NATO held a summit in Brussels, Belgium, where member states discussed increasing defence spending and countering terrorism, with disagreements on display both inside and outside the meeting.

news.title: Accountability Results Announced in Problem Vaccine Case
news.body: Progress was made in the investigation and handling of the Changchun Changsheng problem vaccine case: several people involved were arrested, a number of officials in Jilin were held accountable, and work began on revising vaccine management regulations.

news.title: 'Lunar Palace 365' Experiment Succeeds
news.body: Beihang University's Lunar Palace 365 experiment concluded successfully, with eight volunteers living for 370 consecutive days inside the Lunar Palace 1 module, a world record for the longest and most closed-loop bioregenerative life support experiment.

news.title: Politburo Meeting Sets Tone for Second-Half Economy
news.body: The Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee met to analyse the current economic situation and plan work for the second half of the year, setting out the "six stabilisations" and vowing steady progress in deleveraging.

news.title: Apple's Market Value Tops 1 Trillion Dollars
news.body: Apple's share price hit an intraday record, pushing its market capitalisation past 1 trillion dollars and making it the first US-listed company to reach that level.

news.title: Chinese Military Competes in International Army Games
news.body: Chinese troops travelled to Russia, Kazakhstan and other countries for the 2018 International Army Games, demonstrating solid military skills in competitions across several events.

news.title: Venezuelan President Attacked by Drones
news.body: Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro was targeted by exploding drones while attending an event in the capital Caracas; he was unharmed, in the world's first assassination attempt on a head of state using drones.

news.title: One Year After Jiuzhaigou Quake, Reconstruction Advances
news.body: A year after the magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Jiuzhaigou, Sichuan, infrastructure repairs and ecological restoration in the disaster area were proceeding in an orderly way, and some scenic spots were gradually reopening after rebuilding.

news.title: Film Version of 'iPartment' Draws Criticism
news.body: The film adaptation of the television series iPartment drew a flood of negative reviews for what audiences called false advertising, its rating on Douban fell steadily, and director Wei Zheng spoke out in response to the controversy.

news.title: Qixi Festival Sees Rush of Marriage Registrations
news.body: On the seventh day of the seventh lunar month, marriage registration offices in many parts of the country saw a surge of couples, with many queuing before dawn to obtain their certificates on the traditional festival and commit to each other for life.

news.title: Turkish Lira Plunges
news.body: The Turkish lira fell sharply against the US dollar, sending tremors through emerging markets worldwide, with worsening relations between Turkey and the United States seen as the trigger.

news.title: China Sweeps Both Basketball Golds at Jakarta Asian Games
news.body: Good news came from the basketball courts at the Jakarta Asian Games: China's women's team edged the unified Korean team 71-65 in the final, while the men's team came from behind to beat Iran 84-72 for gold, with Yao Ming watching on as president of the Chinese Basketball Association.

news.title: US and China Impose Tit-for-Tat Tariffs on 16 Billion Dollars of Goods
news.body: The United States began imposing a 25 percent tariff on about 16 billion dollars of Chinese imports, and China took equivalent countermeasures in step, escalating trade friction between the two countries.

news.title: Online Lending Watchdog Issues 108-Item Checklist
news.body: The national office for rectifying online lending issued provinces and cities a notice on compliance inspections of peer-to-peer lending institutions together with a 108-item checklist, unifying compliance standards, subjecting platforms to strict scrutiny and accelerating the shakeout in the industry.

news.title: Another Didi Hitch Killing Prompts Full Overhaul
news.body: A girl was murdered after hailing a Didi Hitch ride in Yueqing, Zhejiang; Didi announced it would take the service offline nationwide and dismissed two senior executives, later rolling out a series of safety measures.

news.title: Preparations Complete for FOCAC Beijing Summit
news.body: Preparations for the Beijing summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation were essentially complete, with the two sides set to discuss cooperation under the theme of "win-win cooperation and joining hands to build an even closer China-Africa community with a shared future".

news.title: Yang Zi and Deng Lun's 'Ashes of Love' Concludes
news.body: The costume fantasy drama Ashes of Love aired its finale, surpassing 10 billion views across online platforms and becoming a phenomenon of the summer season that won both praise and buzz.

news.title: Rumours That 'Jack Ma Is Retiring' Spark Discussion
news.body: Alibaba confirmed that Jack Ma would step down as chairman of the board a year later, with Daniel Zhang taking over, as Ma devotes himself to education and philanthropy, fuelling debate about succession at China's internet giants.

news.title: Syria Tensions Flare Again as Russian Aircraft Shot Down
news.body: During Israeli airstrikes on targets in Syria, a Russian Il-20 reconnaissance plane was mistakenly hit by Syrian air defences and crashed, killing all 15 people aboard and sharply raising tensions between Russia and Israel.

news.title: Typhoon Mangkhut Bears Down on South China
news.body: Super Typhoon Mangkhut formed in the western Pacific and rapidly intensified as it approached China's southern coast, with Guangdong, Guangxi and Hainan on high alert and deploying defences.

news.title: Jack Ma to Step Down as Alibaba Chairman in One Year
news.body: Alibaba founder Jack Ma issued an open letter titled "Happy Teacher's Day", announcing that he would step down as chairman of the board a year later, with CEO Daniel Zhang succeeding him, while he returns to education and philanthropy.

news.title: Russia and Syria Hold Large-Scale Joint Military Drills
news.body: Russia and Syria held large-scale joint military exercises in the Mediterranean involving multiple branches of the armed forces, one of Russia's biggest drills in the region in recent years.

news.title: Apple Unveils iPhone XS Lineup
news.body: At its autumn event, Apple introduced three new phones, the iPhone XS, iPhone XS Max and iPhone XR, with the Max model enlarging the screen to 6.5 inches for the first time.

news.title: Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Other Cities Battle Typhoon Mangkhut
news.body: Super Typhoon Mangkhut made landfall in Taishan, Guangdong, halting work and classes in Shenzhen, Guangzhou and elsewhere; the province evacuated and relocated millions of people, and toppled trees and seawater intrusion caused serious damage in many places.

news.title: NIFA Issues Rules on Fund Custody for P2P Platforms
news.body: The National Internet Finance Association of China issued business and technical standards for fund custody systems in internet peer-to-peer lending, setting unified technical and service benchmarks for bank custody at online lending platforms and supporting compliance rectification in the sector.

news.title: First Chinese Farmers' Harvest Festival Approaches
news.body: With the approval of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council, the autumn equinox of the lunar calendar was designated the Chinese Farmers' Harvest Festival starting in 2018, and celebrations were getting under way across the country ahead of the first such festival.

news.title: Inter-Korean Summit Opens in Pyongyang
news.body: South Korean President Moon Jae-in flew to Pyongyang for his third summit of the year with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, with the two sides exchanging views in depth on denuclearisation of the peninsula and North-South cooperation.

news.title: China's Women Reach Quarterfinals at Basketball World Cup
news.body: At the 2018 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, China beat Latvia, Senegal and other opponents in group play to advance to the last eight, eventually finishing sixth, one of the team's best results at a major tournament in recent years.

news.title: First Week of Hong Kong Section of Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail
news.body: A week after the Hong Kong section of the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link opened, passenger flows at the West Kowloon port were steady and orderly, and travellers praised the co-location immigration arrangement for making border crossing easier.

news.title: National Day Holiday Draws Over 700 Million Tourist Visits
news.body: Over the seven-day National Day holiday in 2018, China received 726 million domestic tourist visits and earned 599.08 billion yuan in domestic tourism revenue, with red tourism and self-drive trips continuing to grow in popularity.

news.title: Powerful Quake and Tsunami in Central Sulawesi, Indonesia, Leave Heavy Toll
news.body: A magnitude-7.4 earthquake struck Central Sulawesi, Indonesia, triggering a tsunami that devastated the city of Palu and left thousands dead or missing, as Chinese rescue teams stood by to help.

news.title: China Beats Thailand 3-0 to Win Women's Volleyball Asian Cup
news.body: In the final of the 2018 Women's Volleyball Asian Cup in Nakhon Ratchasima, Thailand, China swept hosts Thailand in straight sets 3-0 to defend the title.

news.title: CAS and Others Report Progress on New Carbon-Based Chips
news.body: Chinese researchers made important progress in carbon-based nanoelectronic devices, publishing their results in an international academic journal and opening a new path to push past the limits of silicon-based chips.

news.title: Central Campaign Against Organized Crime and Local Mafia Deepens
news.body: The central campaign against organized crime and local mafia-style gangs entered a stage of concentrated effort, with localities digging out the "protective umbrellas" shielding such forces and a number of cases publicly sentenced.

news.title: Turkey Says Saudi Journalist Khashoggi Was Killed
news.body: Turkish authorities disclosed evidence that Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi was killed inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul, causing a strong international reaction and leaving Saudi Arabia under immense diplomatic pressure.

news.title: Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge Officially Opens
news.body: The opening ceremony for the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge was held in Zhuhai, Guangdong, where Xi Jinping attended and declared the bridge officially open; completion of the world's longest sea-crossing bridge sharply cuts travel times between Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao.

news.title: Saudi Arabia Admits for First Time That Khashoggi Died in Consulate
news.body: Saudi Arabia acknowledged for the first time that Khashoggi died in a brawl inside the consulate, and several intelligence officials involved were arrested, as the international community widely demanded a thorough investigation.

news.title: China's First Rail Transit Penalty Rules for Fare Evasion
news.body: A draft regulation on passenger organisation and services for urban rail transit was released for public comment, proposing specific rules to govern behaviour such as eating on the subway and fare evasion.

news.title: China Successfully Launches Haiyang-2B Satellite
news.body: China successfully launched the Haiyang-2B satellite aboard a Long March 4B rocket from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center; the satellite entered its planned orbit, adding a new tool for ocean observation.

news.title: Findings Released in Chongqing Wanzhou Bus Plunge
news.body: The cause of the bus plunge in Wanzhou, Chongqing, was established: a passenger surnamed Liu, who had missed her stop, argued and traded blows with the driver, surnamed Ran, causing the vehicle to veer out of control into the Yangtze River and killing 15 people, a painful lesson that sparked nationwide discussion.

news.title: Central Bank's Reserve Requirement Cut Takes Effect
news.body: The People's Bank of China cut the reserve requirement ratio for some financial institutions by 1 percentage point, releasing about 750 billion yuan in incremental funds that day to support the real economy and inclusive finance.

news.title: Fifth World Internet Conference Opens in Wuzhen
news.body: The fifth World Internet Conference opened in Wuzhen, Zhejiang, under the theme "Creating a Digital World of Mutual Trust and Coexistence", drawing more than 1,500 guests from around the world and releasing a number of leading internet science and technology achievements.

news.title: Democrats Retake House in US Midterm Elections
news.body: Results of the US midterm elections showed the Democrats recapturing a majority in the House of Representatives after eight years, while Republicans held and expanded their Senate advantage, leaving Congress divided.

news.title: 'Double 11' Sales Hit Another Record
news.body: Tmall's gross merchandise volume for the 2018 Double 11 shopping festival reached 213.5 billion yuan for the day, topping 200 billion yuan for the first time, with more than 1 billion logistics orders, while JD.com recorded over 159.8 billion yuan in cumulative orders.

news.title: Centenary of World War I Armistice Commemorated
news.body: Events marking the 100th anniversary of the armistice that ended World War I were held in Paris, attended by leaders from dozens of countries, with many calling for the lessons of history to be remembered and peace upheld.

news.title: First Snowfall of Winter Across Much of China
news.body: A strong cold front swept across central and eastern China, bringing the first snow of the winter to north China, the Huang-Huai region and elsewhere, with temperatures plunging and travel affected to varying degrees.

news.title: 55th Golden Horse Awards Ceremony Held
news.body: The 55th Taiwan Golden Horse Film Awards ceremony was held in Taipei, where Zhang Yimou won best director for Shadow and Xu Zheng and Hsieh Ying-hsuan took the best actor and actress prizes.

news.title: Russia-Ukraine Clash in Kerch Strait
news.body: Russia and Ukraine clashed in the Kerch Strait, with Moscow detaining three Ukrainian warships and their crews; Ukraine declared martial law in some regions as tensions escalated sharply.

news.title: Gene-Edited Babies Case Sparks Outcry Online
news.body: News that "the world's first gene-edited babies were born in China" caused a strong reaction in the scientific community and across society, with 122 scientists signing a joint condemnation and the National Health Commission ordering an investigation in accordance with the law.

news.title: Full Investigation Launched Into Gene-Edited Babies Case
news.body: A Guangdong provincial investigation team concluded that the gene-edited babies project was carried out in blatant violation of laws and regulations, those responsible were dealt with according to law, and He Jiankui faced criminal liability.

news.title: Compliance Checks on Online Lenders Enter Final Stage
news.body: Compliance inspections of online lending platforms around the country entered their closing stage, with regulators requiring self-inspections, industry association reviews and administrative verification to be completed before the end of the year; non-compliant platforms were pushed out faster as the industry consolidated.

news.title: Beijing Shougang Beat Shanghai at Home in CBA Regular Season
news.body: In the 11th round of the CBA regular season, the Beijing Shougang men's team beat the Shanghai Sharks 112-105 at home, with the veteran powerhouse—before Jeremy Lin joined—holding a place near the top of the standings.

news.title: G20 Summit Closes in Argentina
news.body: The 13th G20 Leaders' Summit closed in Buenos Aires, Argentina, adopting the G20 Buenos Aires Leaders' Declaration and reaching consensus on upholding the multilateral trading system.

news.title: China Successfully Launches Saudi Satellites
news.body: China successfully launched the SaudiSat-5A and 5B satellites aboard a Long March 3B rocket from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center, another achievement in China-Saudi space cooperation.

news.title: Widespread Rain, Snow and Falling Temperatures Across China
news.body: A strong cold front affected most of central and eastern China, bringing the heaviest snowfall since the start of winter to many places and sharply lower temperatures, while heating demand in the north peaked.

news.title: Fifth National Memorial Day for Nanjing Massacre Victims
news.body: The national memorial ceremony for the victims of the Nanjing Massacre was held at the Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders, with those present observing a moment of silence as air-raid sirens sounded across Nanjing.

news.title: UK PM Theresa May Survives No-Confidence Vote
news.body: British Prime Minister Theresa May survived a no-confidence vote within the Conservative Party by 200 votes to 117, keeping both her party leadership and her premiership, though the Brexit process remained deadlocked.

news.title: Symposium Held on Special Campaign Against P2P Lending Risks
news.body: The national leading group for the special campaign against P2P online lending risks held a symposium that set the overall direction of "exit wherever possible and shut down wherever necessary" for online lenders, guiding the vast majority of platforms to wind down voluntarily and speeding up the resolution of legacy risks.

news.title: US Announces Withdrawal of Troops From Syria
news.body: US President Donald Trump announced that American forces would withdraw from Syria, causing shock at home and abroad, and Defense Secretary Jim Mattis resigned shortly afterwards.

news.title: Guangdong Rout Beijing in CBA 'Jing-Yue' Clash
news.body: The 22nd round of the CBA regular season featured the classic Beijing-Guangdong clash, in which the Guangdong Dongguan Bank men's team won 96-87 away to Beijing Shougang and led the standings on a long winning streak, with Yi Jianlian's steady play carrying his team through.

news.title: Conference Marking 40 Years of Reform and Opening Up Held
news.body: A conference celebrating the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, reviewing four decades of achievement, honouring reform pioneers and declaring the resolve to press ahead with reform.

news.title: BeiDou-3 Basic System Completed for Global Service
news.body: The China Satellite Navigation Office announced that the basic BeiDou-3 system had been completed and would provide global services from that day, taking China's BeiDou into a global era.

news.title: 2019 Spring Festival Travel Plan for National Railways Released
news.body: The 2019 Spring Festival travel plan was released, with the national railway expected to carry 413 million passenger trips, and tickets for peak periods before and after the holiday selling out within seconds of going on sale.

news.title: New Year's Eve Events Held Across China
news.body: On the last night of 2018, Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Chengdu and other cities held New Year's light shows and countdown events, with tens of thousands of residents welcoming 2019 amid laughter and good wishes.

news.title: Gas Explosion in Apartment Block in Russia's Far East
news.body: A gas explosion collapsed part of a residential building in Magnitogorsk, Russia, killing dozens of people, as rescue work proceeded with difficulty in freezing temperatures.

news.title: First Day of 2019 Spring Festival Travel Rush
news.body: The 2019 Spring Festival travel rush officially began, with the national railway expected to carry a record 413 million passenger trips, and reverse-direction travel and e-tickets emerging as new trends.

news.title: Japan's Hayabusa2 Touches Down on Asteroid a Second Time
news.body: Japan's Hayabusa2 probe successfully touched down on the asteroid Ryugu for a second time and completed sampling, a key step towards unlocking the mystery of the solar system's origins.

news.title: Watchdogs Order Checks on Illegal Cash-Loan Platforms
news.body: The office of the leading group for the special campaign against internet finance risks and the office of the leading group for the special campaign against P2P lending risks issued a joint notice requiring localities to investigate illegal online loan facilitation and cooperation between licensed financial institutions and cash-loan platforms, in a bid to strictly prevent illegal lending.

news.title: Investigation Into Quanjian Case Advances
news.body: The investigation and handling of Quanjian over suspected pyramid selling and false advertising continued, with the company's de facto controller Shu Yuhui and others arrested in accordance with the law, alongside a campaign to clean up chaos in the health supplements market.

news.title: Nadal Sweeps Tsitsipas 3-0 in Australian Open Semifinal
news.body: In the men's singles semifinal at the Australian Open, Spain's Rafael Nadal swept Greek rising star Stefanos Tsitsipas 3-0 without dropping a set to reach the final and take aim at his 18th Grand Slam title.

news.title: Pre-Holiday Travel Peak Begins
news.body: The Spring Festival travel rush entered its pre-holiday peak, with the national railway carrying more than 10 million passengers a day for several days running; extra trains were added and major stations activated emergency plans for large passenger flows.

news.title: Political Crisis Erupts in Venezuela
news.body: Venezuelan opposition leader Juan Guaido declared himself interim president, the United States and other countries quickly recognised him, and President Nicolas Maduro announced the severing of diplomatic ties with Washington, plunging Venezuelan politics into turmoil.

news.title: Gaokao Syllabus Released as Reforms Advance
news.body: The Ministry of Education released the 2019 gaokao examination syllabus as many parts of the country pushed ahead with comprehensive reform of the college entrance exam, tightening the independent admissions policy and cracking down on fraud.

news.title: 2018 Economic Data Released, GDP Grows 6.6 Percent
news.body: The National Bureau of Statistics reported that China's gross domestic product surpassed 90 trillion yuan in 2018, growing 6.6 percent year on year and meeting the target of around 6.5 percent growth.

news.title: After First-Ever Far-Side Landing, Chang'e-4 Runs Biology Experiment
news.body: The Chang'e-4 mission team announced that a biological experiment payload aboard the probe had successfully sprouted seedlings on the far side of the Moon, the first plant shoots ever grown there.

news.title: 2019 Spring Festival Holiday Begins
news.body: On the last working day before Lunar New Year's Eve, cross-regional travel across the country peaked, and on New Year's Eve the national railway set a single-day record for passenger trips during the Spring Festival travel rush.

news.title: CCTV Spring Festival Gala Programme List Announced for 2019
news.body: The programme list for CCTV's 2019 Spring Festival Gala, marking the Year of the Pig, was officially announced, with song-and-dance and comedy acts offering plenty of highlights and the main Beijing venue linked with three satellite stages.

news.title: A Look at National Tourism Spending Over the Spring Festival Holiday
news.body: Over the seven-day Spring Festival holiday, China received 415 million tourist visits and earned 513.9 billion yuan in tourism revenue, with folk culture tours and snow-and-ice trips proving popular.

news.title: US Begins Process of Withdrawing From INF Treaty
news.body: The United States announced it was suspending its obligations under the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty and starting the withdrawal process, and Russia responded with reciprocal measures, putting the global arms control system to the test.

news.title: 'The Wandering Earth' Leads Spring Festival Box Office
news.body: The Chinese science fiction film The Wandering Earth, adapted from Liu Cixin's novel of the same name, won rave reviews for its hard sci-fi production and patriotic feeling, eventually grossing more than 4.6 billion yuan and being hailed as opening the first year of Chinese science fiction cinema.

news.title: CCTV Spring Festival Gala Sets Ratings Record
news.body: The 2019 CCTV Spring Festival Gala drew a total audience of more than 1.1 billion at home and abroad, a new high in recent years, with clips of several performances flooding social media.

news.title: Durant Leads Warriors in 2019 NBA All-Star Game
news.body: The 2019 NBA All-Star Game was played in Charlotte, where Team LeBron beat Team Giannis 178-164 and Kevin Durant scored 31 points to be named All-Star Game MVP.

news.title: Post-Holiday Return Travel Stays Heavy
news.body: After the Spring Festival holiday ended, the national railway saw return passenger flows remain at a sustained peak, with family visits, students and migrant workers all travelling around the Lantern Festival.

news.title: State Council Issues Outline for Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area
news.body: The Outline Development Plan for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area was officially released, setting the goal of building a world-class bay area and city cluster, as development of the Greater Bay Area entered a stage of full implementation.

news.title: India and Pakistan Clash in Air Battle
news.body: India and Pakistan engaged in an aerial battle near the Line of Control in Kashmir, with each side losing fighter jets; Pakistan's release of a captured Indian pilot eased tensions.

news.title: Chinese Scientists' Chang'e-4 Far-Side Findings Published in Nature
news.body: Research by Chinese scientists based on data from the Chang'e-4 probe was published online in the top international journal Nature, revealing the subsurface layering beneath the Von Karman crater on the far side of the Moon.

news.title: Chinese and Foreign Media Focus on Beijing Ahead of Two Sessions
news.body: With the 2019 Two Sessions about to open, Chinese and foreign journalists arrived in Beijing to register, with livelihood issues such as employment, education and healthcare in the spotlight before the meetings.

news.title: PBOC Leads Push to Improve Long-Term Internet Finance Supervision
news.body: The People's Bank of China, together with relevant departments, is studying a long-term mechanism for supervising internet finance, setting access and rectification requirements for internet finance institutions and pressing ahead with a campaign against online lending risks to prevent any resurgence.

news.title: Second Trump-Kim Summit Ends Without Agreement
news.body: US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un held their second meeting in Hanoi, Vietnam, but failed to reach an agreement over sanctions and denuclearisation, and the talks ended early.

news.title: China's Two Sessions Set to Open
news.body: With the 2019 Two Sessions about to begin, nearly 3,000 NPC deputies and more than 2,100 CPPCC members arrived in Beijing, with poverty alleviation and improving the business environment in focus.

news.title: Indian Jets Strike Targets Inside Pakistan
news.body: Indian Air Force jets crossed the border and struck targets inside Pakistan, saying they hit facilities of terrorist groups; Pakistan lodged a strong protest as tensions in South Asia escalated sharply.

news.title: Saluting 'She Power' on Women's Day
news.body: On International Women's Day, people across the country paid tribute to women workers in many forms, with women's contributions in scientific research, spaceflight and poverty alleviation drawing wide attention.

news.title: Venezuela's Massive Blackout Crisis
news.body: A nationwide blackout hit Venezuela, paralysing the capital Caracas and other major cities; the government blamed the opposition for sabotage as the situation grew more unstable.

news.title: Ethiopian Airlines Passenger Jet Crashes
news.body: A Boeing 737-8 operated by Ethiopian Airlines crashed shortly after takeoff, killing all 157 people on board, including eight Chinese citizens, raising strong global doubts about the safety of the Boeing 737 MAX.

news.title: UK House of Commons Rejects Brexit Deal Again
news.body: The House of Commons rejected the Brexit deal again by 391 votes to 242, dealing another heavy blow to Prime Minister Theresa May's withdrawal plan.

news.title: Countries Around the World Ground Boeing 737 MAX
news.body: After the Ethiopian Airlines crash, China became the first to ground the Boeing 737-8 and dozens of countries and regions followed by grounding the 737 MAX; the United States announced a grounding last, leaving Boeing in an unprecedented crisis of confidence.

news.title: 3.15 Gala Exposes E-Cigarettes, Wi-Fi Probe Boxes and More
news.body: CCTV's annual 3.15 consumer rights gala exposed a black-market medical waste industry, irregularities at online lending platforms such as Rong360, and the dangers of e-cigarettes; several companies involved responded overnight and pledged to rectify the problems.

news.title: CBA: Guangdong Beat Liaoning in Marquee Showdown
news.body: The 45th round of the CBA regular season produced a marquee Liaoning-Guangdong clash, in which Guangdong Dongguan Bank beat Liaoning Benxi Steel 127-103 at home, sweeping the season series and clinching the regular-season title.

news.title: Revised 2018 GDP Figures Released
news.body: The National Bureau of Statistics announced that, after final verification, China's 2018 gross domestic product was revised upward from the preliminary figure, taking the economy's total size to a new level.

news.title: Martyrs of Muli Forest Fire in Liangshan Laid to Rest
news.body: The ashes of 30 firefighters who died heroically battling a forest fire in Muli County, Liangshan Prefecture, Sichuan, were returned and buried; the dead included 27 forest firefighting officers and personnel and three local officials and residents, as the nation mourned and paid tribute to the heroes.

news.title: China Successfully Launches BeiDou-3 IGSO Satellite
news.body: China launched its 46th BeiDou navigation satellite on a Long March 3B carrier rocket from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center, steadily advancing the BeiDou-3 constellation.

news.title: Event Horizon Announcement: Public Riveted by Black Hole Photo
news.body: The Event Horizon Telescope project held simultaneous press conferences in six locations worldwide to release the first-ever photograph of a black hole, letting the world 'see' a black hole for the first time and sparking a nationwide wave of enthusiasm for science.

news.title: Military Coup in Sudan
news.body: Sudan's military staged a coup to overthrow President Omar al-Bashir, who had ruled for 30 years, and then set up a transitional military council to take over the country, with tensions high in the capital Khartoum.

news.title: First-Ever Image of a Black Hole Released Worldwide
news.body: The Shanghai Astronomical Observatory of the Chinese Academy of Sciences released humanity's first image of a black hole in coordination with the rest of the world; the image, of the black hole at the centre of the galaxy M87 in Virgo, confirmed predictions of Einstein's general theory of relativity.

news.title: Fighting Escalates in Libya
news.body: Libya's National Army and forces of the Government of National Accord fought fierce battles on the outskirts of the capital Tripoli; the United Nations called for a ceasefire as the humanitarian situation deteriorated.

news.title: World Book Day Marked with Reading Events
news.body: Around World Book Day on April 23, book-sharing sessions, classic recitals and other events were held widely across the country, as reading for all became a popular trend.

news.title: China Successfully Launches Tianhui-2 01 Satellites
news.body: China launched the Tianhui-2 01 group of satellites on a Long March 4B carrier rocket from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, and the satellites entered their planned orbits.

news.title: CSL Title Clash: Guoan Edge Evergrande 1-0
news.body: In a top-of-the-table clash in the sixth round of the Chinese Super League, Beijing Sinobo Guoan beat Guangzhou Evergrande Taobao 1-0 at home with a goal from Jonathan Viera, making it six wins from six to lead the standings.

news.title: String of Bombings in Sri Lanka Causes Heavy Casualties
news.body: A series of bomb attacks struck the Sri Lankan capital Colombo and other areas, targeting churches and luxury hotels, killing more than 250 people and injuring over 500 in an attack that shocked the world.

news.title: Second Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation Held
news.body: The second Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation was held in Beijing, attended by leaders of 40 countries and international organisations; the roundtable summit adopted a joint communique and produced 283 practical cooperation outcomes.

news.title: Beijing Horticultural Expo Set to Open
news.body: On the eve of the 2019 International Horticultural Exhibition in Beijing, all preparations were complete, with 110 countries and international organisations confirmed as participants as the expo prepared to welcome visitors from around the world.

news.title: Beijing Horticultural Expo Officially Opens
news.body: The 2019 International Horticultural Exhibition opened in Yanqing, Beijing, under the theme 'Live Green, Live Better', bringing together the world's finest horticulture and drawing large crowds on its first day.

news.title: Japan's Emperor Akihito Abdicates
news.body: Japan's Emperor Akihito formally abdicated, ending the 30-year Heisei era; Crown Prince Naruhito ascended the throne on May 1, ushering in Japan's Reiwa era.

news.title: Japan's Reiwa Era Begins
news.body: Japan's new emperor, Naruhito, took the throne and Japan entered the Reiwa era, with the international community watching closely how the country's domestic and foreign policies would evolve in the new era.

news.title: Extended May Day Holiday Fuels Travel Boom
news.body: The 2019 May Day holiday was extended to four days, with 195 million domestic tourist trips nationwide generating 117.67 billion yuan in tourism revenue, as short trips and high-speed rail travel proved the big draw.

news.title: Failed Mutiny in Venezuela
news.body: A small-scale mutiny took place in Venezuela, with opposition and government supporters facing off in the streets of the capital; the government quickly took control, but the political deadlock continued.

news.title: China Launches Multiple Satellites on Long March 4C
news.body: China successfully launched several satellites on a Long March 4C carrier rocket from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, marking complete success for the mission.

news.title: Farmers Busy as Start of Summer Arrives
news.body: With the arrival of the Start of Summer solar term, major producing areas entered a critical period for field management of summer-harvest crops, and farmers rushed to carry out pest and disease control.

news.title: Building Collapse in Kenyan Capital
news.body: A building under construction collapsed in the Kenyan capital Nairobi, causing casualties, as rescuers carried out an intense search in the rubble.

news.title: Iran Suspends Some Commitments Under Nuclear Deal
news.body: Iranian President Hassan Rouhani announced that Iran would suspend some of its commitments under the Iran nuclear deal and issued a 60-day ultimatum to European countries, escalating tensions in the Middle East.

news.title: Conference on Dialogue of Asian Civilizations to Be Held in Beijing
news.body: On the eve of the Conference on Dialogue of Asian Civilizations, preparations were complete, with representatives of 47 Asian countries and countries beyond the region set to gather in Beijing to discuss exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations.

news.title: Conference on Dialogue of Asian Civilizations Opens
news.body: The Conference on Dialogue of Asian Civilizations opened in Beijing, where President Xi Jinping attended the opening ceremony and delivered a keynote speech calling for mutual respect, equality and stronger exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations.

news.title: China's First Domestically Built Aircraft Carrier Completes Sea Trials
news.body: China's first domestically built aircraft carrier returned to its Dalian berth after completing its fifth sea trial, during which it tested aircraft-ship compatibility, at-sea replenishment and other items, moving a step closer to commissioning.

news.title: Liverpool Beat Tottenham 2-0 to Win Champions League
news.body: The 2018-19 UEFA Champions League final was played at the Wanda Metropolitano in Madrid, where Liverpool beat Tottenham 2-0 with a Mohamed Salah penalty and a goal from Divock Origi to lift the trophy for the sixth time in club history.

news.title: MIIT Poised to Issue 5G Commercial Licences
news.body: With the issuance of 5G commercial licences imminent, the three major telecom operators were building 5G trial networks in several cities, while 5G handsets and pricing plans became a focus for consumers.

news.title: MIIT Officially Issues 5G Commercial Licences
news.body: The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology issued 5G commercial licences to China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom and China Broadcasting Network, formally beginning China's first year of 5G commercialisation and bringing historic opportunities to the telecom supply chain.

news.title: Sharp Swings in London Stocks and Bonds
news.body: Amid global trade tensions, major European stock and bond markets saw heightened volatility as investors turned more risk-averse.

news.title: World Environment Day Host Event Held in Hangzhou
news.body: The global host event for World Environment Day 2019 was held in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, focusing on tackling air pollution, as China released its Air Quality Improvement Report (2013-2018).

news.title: St. Petersburg International Economic Forum Held
news.body: The St. Petersburg International Economic Forum took place, with political leaders and business executives from many countries discussing the main challenges facing the world economy and opportunities for cooperation.

news.title: Gaokao Ends as Provinces Announce Score Release Dates
news.body: China's 2019 national college entrance examination concluded smoothly, with many provinces announcing when scores would be released and how applications would be organised, alongside a flurry of application advisory services and warnings.

news.title: Tanker Attacks in the Gulf of Oman
news.body: Two tankers were attacked and set ablaze in the Gulf of Oman; the United States blamed Iran, which vehemently denied the accusation, fuelling fresh tension in the Gulf and pushing international oil prices higher.

news.title: President Xi Arrives in Dushanbe for CICA Summit
news.body: President Xi Jinping arrived in Dushanbe to attend the fifth summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia and to pay a state visit to Tajikistan, promoting the building of an Asian community with a shared future.

news.title: CBIRC Cracks Down on Chaos in Online Lending
news.body: The China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission held a meeting stressing continued action against irregularities in online lending and other internet finance, strict investigation of cooperation between licensed institutions and illegal online lending platforms, protection of financial consumers' rights and defusing of internet finance risks.

news.title: Raptors Beat Warriors 4-2 for First NBA Title
news.body: In Game 6 of the NBA Finals, the Toronto Raptors won 114-110 on the road against the Golden State Warriors to take the series 4-2 and claim the franchise's first NBA championship; Kawhi Leonard was named Finals MVP as the Warriors' dynasty was hit hard by injuries.

news.title: President Xi Jinping Visits North Korea
news.body: Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and president of China, arrived in Pyongyang on a special plane for a state visit to North Korea, the first visit by China's top party and state leader in 14 years.

news.title: 2019 Summer Davos Ready to Open
news.body: The 2019 Summer Davos forum was about to be held in Dalian under the theme 'Leadership 4.0: Succeeding in a New Era of Globalisation', with political and business leaders from around the world set to gather in the coastal city.

news.title: Expectations of a Fed Rate Cut Grow
news.body: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said the Fed would act as appropriate to sustain the economic expansion, sharply raising market expectations of a rate cut and lifting stock markets around the world.

news.title: Shanghai First to Enforce Mandatory Household Waste Sorting
news.body: The Shanghai Municipal Regulation on Domestic Waste Management took effect, making Shanghai the first city to enter an era of mandatory household waste sorting, with individuals who mix their waste facing fines of up to 200 yuan and the public taking 'waste sorting demonstration lessons'.

news.title: Iran Breaches Uranium Enrichment Limit
news.body: Iran announced it had exceeded the 3.67% uranium enrichment limit set by the Iran nuclear deal, prompting emergency consultations among the European parties, which urged Iran to reverse the move as tensions over the Middle East nuclear issue remained high.

news.title: Dalian Enforces Mandatory Waste Sorting
news.body: Dalian followed suit in enforcing mandatory household waste sorting, issuing fines to organisations and individuals that failed to sort properly, as the list of cities moving from encouraging sorting to making it mandatory kept growing.

news.title: China Successfully Launches Jixing-1 02 Satellite
news.body: China launched the Yaogan-32 01 group of satellites and others on a Long March 3B carrier rocket from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center, and the satellites entered their planned orbits.

news.title: Fire on Russian Submersible Kills 14
news.body: A fire broke out on a Russian deep-diving submersible in the Barents Sea, killing 14 crew members, including several senior officers; the nation mourned after the Russian Defence Ministry disclosed the news.

news.title: 2019 Gaokao Admissions Begin
news.body: University admissions for the 2019 gaokao got under way across China's provinces, with early-batch and undergraduate-batch applications processed in order and special programmes favouring candidates from rural and impoverished areas.

news.title: STAR Market Ready to Open
news.body: The first 25 STAR Market companies confirmed their listing schedules, with more than 3.8 million investors having opened trading permissions, as China's capital market reached a historic moment.

news.title: Trump Threatens Tariffs on French Goods
news.body: Because France planned to impose a digital tax on internet giants, US President Donald Trump threatened to impose additional tariffs on French wine and other goods exported to the United States, heating up US-EU trade friction.

news.title: CBA Summer League and Yangtze Delta Tournament in Full Swing
news.body: The 2019 CBA Summer League and Yangtze River Delta Professional Basketball Club Challenge were fiercely contested in Shanghai, with several CBA teams using games to train and assess new players while China's national team made its final preparations for the FIBA World Cup at home. In this game, Jiangsu beat Shenzhen.

news.title: 'Big-Head Baby' Case Prompts Dairy Industry Self-Inspection
news.body: A case in Chenzhou, Hunan, in which solid beverages were passed off as special medical-purpose infant formula, continued to draw attention; the State Administration for Market Regulation launched a campaign against solid drinks sold as special medical food, and several provinces began screening.

news.title: Boris Johnson Becomes UK Prime Minister
news.body: Boris Johnson formally took office as British prime minister and formed a new cabinet, stressing that Britain must leave the EU by October 31, while the EU said there was limited room to restart negotiations.

news.title: Sustained Heatwave Hits Much of China
news.body: The National Meteorological Center issued consecutive heat warnings as temperatures in many southern areas broke historic records and electricity loads hit new highs, with authorities working to ensure power supply through the summer peak.

news.title: Typhoon Lekima Approaches East China
news.body: Super Typhoon Lekima approached the coast of East China; the National Meteorological Center issued a red typhoon alert, hundreds of thousands of people were evacuated in Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu, and many train services and flights were cancelled.

news.title: China Successfully Launches Qiancheng-1 01 Satellite
news.body: China launched the Qiancheng-1 01 satellite and others on a Long March 2C carrier rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, marking new progress in commercial space launches.

news.title: Typhoon Lekima Makes Landfall in Zhejiang
news.body: This year's No. 9 typhoon, Lekima, made landfall in Wenling, Zhejiang, with maximum winds near its centre of force 16 at landfall, making it the strongest typhoon to hit China this year and causing severe wind and rain damage in many places.

news.title: Tensions Persist in Indian Kashmir
news.body: After India announced the revocation of the special status of Indian-administered Kashmir, the region remained under lockdown, with Pakistan strongly opposed and downgrading bilateral ties.

news.title: China's Table Tennis Olympic Simulation in Full Swing
news.body: The Chinese table tennis team's Tokyo Olympic simulation tournament was in full swing in Lingshui, Hainan, with the full squad of top players taking part, including Ma Long, Fan Zhendong and Chen Meng, under rules matching the Tokyo Olympics. In this match, Chen Meng beat Sun Yingsha.

news.title: Palace Museum's First Night Opening Sparks Ticket Rush
news.body: For the first time in its 94-year history, the Palace Museum opened at night, and reservations for the 'Lantern Festival Night' light show sold out within seconds, drawing nationwide attention.

news.title: Beijing Daxing International Airport Conducts Test Flights
news.body: Beijing Daxing International Airport carried out completion inspections and test flights, with airliners from several carriers successfully completing trial flights, as the world's largest single-terminal airport prepared to begin operations.

news.title: G7 Summit Opens in France
news.body: The G7 summit opened in Biarritz, France, with climate change, trade disputes and Iran topping the agenda; the summit issued no joint communique.

news.title: G7 Summit Closes with Divisions Unresolved
news.body: The G7 summit closed without issuing a joint communique, a rare omission that laid bare deep divisions among major Western countries over trade, climate change and other issues.

news.title: State Council Meeting Plans Deeper Administrative Reform, Backs Orderly Internet Finance
news.body: An executive meeting of the State Council stressed the need to speed up a long-term mechanism for supervising internet finance, to tighten access and rectification in online lending and other fields, and to support private capital entering the financial sector in an orderly way.

news.title: Beijing Daxing International Airport Counts Down to Opening
news.body: Beijing Daxing International Airport completed its completion inspection and was due to begin formal operations before the end of September, taking Beijing into an era of twin aviation hubs.

news.title: China Successfully Launches ChinaSat-18 Satellite
news.body: China successfully launched the ChinaSat-18 communications satellite on a Long March 3B carrier rocket from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center, and the satellite entered its planned orbit.

news.title: New School Term Begins Smoothly Nationwide
news.body: Primary and secondary schools opened smoothly for the autumn term across the country, with many places holding a 'first lesson of the term' and the Ministry of Education expanding and improving after-school services to ease the burden on parents.

news.title: UK Commons Passes Bill to Block No-Deal Brexit
news.body: The House of Commons passed a bill requiring the prime minister to write to the EU requesting an extension if no Brexit deal is reached by October 19, dealing a heavy blow to Boris Johnson's government.

news.title: Beijing Daxing International Airport Officially Opens
news.body: Beijing Daxing International Airport officially began operations, with Xi Jinping attending the ceremony and declaring the airport open; the 'phoenix spreading its wings' became a new landmark for the capital.

news.title: Johnson's Suspension of Parliament Sparks Controversy
news.body: Prime Minister Boris Johnson's decision to suspend Parliament led to legal action at Britain's Supreme Court and protests by tens of thousands on the streets, as the Brexit process lurched from one setback to another.

news.title: China Beat Maldives 5-0 in World Cup Qualifier
news.body: In the second round of Asian qualifying for the 2022 World Cup, China's men's team won 5-0 away to the Maldives, with goals from Wu Xi, Wu Lei, Yang Xu and Elkeson, getting their qualifying campaign off to a winning start.

news.title: Traditional Culture Thrives as Mid-Autumn Festival Nears
news.body: As the Mid-Autumn Festival approached, places across the country held traditional folk activities such as making mooncakes, admiring lanterns and moon worship, as interest in traditional culture kept growing and simple gift boxes became the norm in the mooncake market.

news.title: Beijing Horticultural Expo Closes
news.body: The 2019 International Horticultural Exhibition in Beijing closed after 162 days, having welcomed nearly 10 million visitors and hosted more than 10,000 cultural events, writing a vivid chapter on 'living green'.

news.title: Saudi Aramco Oil Facilities Attacked
news.body: Two oil facilities of Saudi Aramco were attacked by drones, halving Saudi Arabia's daily crude output, equivalent to about 5% of global daily supply, and sending international oil prices soaring by a record margin in a single day.

news.title: Beijing Daxing Airport Expressway Fully Opens
news.body: With the opening of Beijing Daxing International Airport, the supporting expressway and the Daxing Airport Express rail line opened fully, with the fastest journey from Caoqiao Station to the airport taking just 19 minutes.

news.title: US House Launches Trump Impeachment Inquiry
news.body: US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi announced that the House would launch an impeachment inquiry into President Donald Trump, accusing him of pressuring Ukraine to investigate a political rival, throwing US politics into turmoil.

news.title: Reception Marks 70th Anniversary of the People's Republic
news.body: A reception celebrating the 70th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China was held at the Great Hall of the People, where Xi Jinping and other party and state leaders joined Chinese and foreign guests in marking the occasion.

news.title: China Launches Weili Space BeiDou Companion Satellites
news.body: China successfully launched several satellites, including the Weili Space BeiDou companion satellite, on a Long March 11 carrier rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, another success for the solid-fuelled launch vehicle.

news.title: Reviewing the 2019 National Day Holiday
news.body: During the seven-day National Day holiday in 2019, China received 782 million domestic tourist trips and earned 649.71 billion yuan in domestic tourism revenue, with red tourism and the nighttime economy the highlights.

news.title: Turkey Strikes Kurdish Forces in Northern Syria
news.body: Turkish troops crossed into northern Syria and launched a military operation against the Kurdish People's Protection Units, sharply worsening the situation in Syria and drawing condemnation from many countries.

news.title: China Held 0-0 by Philippines in World Cup Qualifier
news.body: In the second round of Asian qualifying for the 2022 World Cup, China's men's team was held to a 0-0 draw away to the Philippines, with Yang Xu and Wu Lei spurning several chances, clouding the team's prospects of advancing from the group.

news.title: China's Mars Probe Makes Public Debut
news.body: China's first Mars landing and obstacle-avoidance hovering test was successfully conducted in Huailai, Hebei, where the country's Mars probe made its first public appearance and was named Tianwen-1.

news.title: Seventh Military World Games Set to Open
news.body: The torch relay for the seventh CISM Military World Games finished in Wuhan ahead of the opening ceremony on the 18th, where more than 9,300 military athletes from 109 countries will compete; it is the first time the Games have been held in China.

news.title: UK and EU Reach New Brexit Deal
news.body: Britain and the EU reached a new Brexit agreement, but the British Parliament postponed its vote and the Brexit deadline was extended again, leaving the deadlock unbroken.

news.title: China Dominates Military World Games Medal Table
news.body: Halfway through the Wuhan Military World Games, China led the gold and overall medal tables by a wide margin, with Bayi teams in shooting, swimming and military pentathlon repeatedly breaking Games records.

news.title: Brexit Delayed Yet Again
news.body: The EU agreed to a flexible extension of Brexit to January 31, 2020, and the British Parliament was dissolved early, with a general election in December to break the deadlock.

news.title: Poverty Alleviation Push in Liangshan, Guizhou
news.body: China's poverty alleviation effort entered its final sprint, with several deeply impoverished counties declaring they had shaken off poverty and localities reviewing their work, making the prevention of a return to poverty a priority.

news.title: ISIS Leader al-Baghdadi Killed in US Operation
news.body: The United States announced that Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, the top leader of the extremist group Islamic State, died by detonating a suicide vest during a US raid in northwestern Syria, drawing reactions from many countries.

news.title: 'Double 11' Presales Begin
news.body: Presales for the 2019 'Double 11' shopping festival began, with the livestreams of Li Jiaqi and Viya drawing more than 100 million views each; livestream selling became a new engine of consumption, and many brands exceeded last year's full-day sales on the first day of presales.

news.title: California Wildfires Keep Spreading
news.body: Wildfires kept spreading in California, forcing nearly 200,000 people to evacuate; the governor declared a state of emergency as strong winds hampered firefighting efforts.

news.title: Fourth Plenary Session of 19th CPC Central Committee Held in Beijing
news.body: The fourth plenary session of the 19th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China was held in Beijing and adopted a decision on upholding and improving the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and modernising China's system and capacity for governance.

news.title: Political Upheaval in Bolivia
news.body: Mass protests erupted in Bolivia, and President Evo Morales announced his resignation on the advice of the military and travelled to Mexico to seek asylum, as turmoil in several Latin American countries reshaped the region.

news.title: China International Import Expo Opens in Shanghai
news.body: The second China International Import Expo opened in Shanghai, with 181 countries, regions and international organisations taking part and more than 3,800 companies exhibiting, as China opened its doors wider to the world.

news.title: Chile Abandons Plan to Host APEC Leaders' Meeting
news.body: Citing domestic unrest, Chile announced it would not host the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting or the climate change conference, drawing regret from the international community as it looked for alternatives.

news.title: Venice Hit by Severe Flooding
news.body: Venice suffered its worst flooding in more than half a century, with landmarks including St. Mark's Square submerged; the mayor said the damage was severe as the world watched the fate of the World Heritage city.

news.title: Flu Season Arrives Across China
news.body: Local disease control authorities issued warnings as China entered peak flu season, with demand for flu vaccinations surging and vaccine shortages reported in some places at certain times.

news.title: Third CIIE Closes with Record Deals
news.body: The second China International Import Expo closed with intended deals worth 71.13 billion US dollars, up 23% from the first edition, as an open Chinese market injected vitality into the world economy.

news.title: Regulators Say Online Lending Platforms Should Exit Where Possible
news.body: The national internet finance rectification office held a meeting reiterating that the campaign against online lending would continue with undiminished intensity, that the vast majority of online lending institutions would be guided to wind down in batches, and that existing business would be handled in accordance with the law to protect lenders' legitimate rights.

news.title: First Major Snowfall of Winter Hits Many Areas
news.body: A strong cold front swept across central and eastern China, bringing the first widespread snowfall of the winter to many parts of northern and northeastern China; temperatures dropped sharply and sanitation and traffic authorities cleared snow overnight to keep roads open.

news.title: Political Turmoil Continues in Bolivia
news.body: Bolivia's interim government announced it was breaking off diplomatic relations with Cuba, and interim President Jeanine Anez took office, with social confrontation persisting and the political outlook still unclear.

news.title: China Lose 1-2 to Syria in World Cup Qualifier
news.body: In the second round of Asian qualifying for the 2022 World Cup, China's men's team lost 1-2 away to Syria, falling five points behind the group leaders and putting their hopes of advancing in jeopardy; national team coach Marcello Lippi resigned after the match.

news.title: First-Instance Verdict in Gene-Edited Babies Case
news.body: A Shenzhen court delivered a first-instance verdict in the 'gene-edited babies' case, holding He Jiankui and two others criminally responsible for illegal medical practice, once again underscoring the ethical bottom line in scientific research.

news.title: New Beijing Subway Lines Near Opening
news.body: Beijing's new airport express line and the eastern extension of Line 7 and southern extension of the Batong Line entered the final stage before opening, with several new subway lines due to open around the end of the year.

news.title: NATO Summit Held in London
news.body: A summit marking NATO's 70th anniversary was held in London, where member states coordinated positions on defence spending and counterterrorism, though internal divisions remained.

news.title: National Constitution Publicity Week Held
news.body: Around the sixth National Constitution Day, Constitution Publicity Week events were held across the country, with campaigns taking the Constitution into companies, schools and communities.

news.title: Iran Acknowledges Some Details on Downed Ukrainian Jet
news.body: The international community continued to follow the crash of the Ukrainian airliner, with many countries demanding that Iran thoroughly investigate the truth as Middle East tensions gripped the world.

news.title: Spring Festival Travel Tickets Go on Sale
news.body: Tickets for the 2020 Spring Festival travel rush went on sale, with Chinese New Year's Eve the most sought-after date; the waitlist booking feature was rolled out nationwide and e-tickets covered most high-speed rail lines.

news.title: Conservative Landslide in UK General Election
news.body: Britain held a general election and Boris Johnson's Conservative Party won an absolute majority in the House of Commons, clearing the way for Britain to leave the EU on schedule as the pound surged.

news.title: CBA: Guangdong Rout Shandong 127-96
news.body: In the 20th round of the CBA regular season, defending champions Guangdong Dongguan Bank won 127-96 away to Shandong, extending their winning streak and staying top of the standings as MarShon Brooks scored a game-high total.

news.title: Macao Marks 20 Years Since Return to China
news.body: A ceremony marking the 20th anniversary of Macao's return to China and the inauguration of the fifth-term government of the Macao Special Administrative Region was held, with Xi Jinping attending and delivering an important speech.

news.title: Railways Unveil 2020 Spring Festival Travel Plan
news.body: The 2020 Spring Festival travel rush was to begin on January 10, with railways nationwide expected to carry a record 440 million passengers as student and migrant worker travel overlapped heavily before the holiday.

news.title: Car Bomb Attack in Somali Capital
news.body: A car bomb attack in the Somali capital Mogadishu killed and injured dozens, as militant activity once again threatened regional security.

news.title: 2019 Year-in-Review Posts Flood Social Media
news.body: On the last night of 2019, year-in-review features, New Year's Eve galas and light shows on various platforms accompanied hundreds of millions of netizens in bidding farewell to the old year and welcoming the 2020s.

news.title: Fireworks Ring In the New Year in Cities Worldwide
news.body: Sydney, London, Dubai and many other cities around the world staged New Year's Eve fireworks displays, with millions of people welcoming 2020 on site or via livestreams.
